definition_zh: 运动员；播放器；演奏者；参与者
definition_en: someone who takes part in a game or sport; also a device that plays recorded sound, a musician, or an active participant in a situation
core_image: 一个人站在场地中央，脚下有球，身后是等着看他下一步动作的观众
scene: 球场的看台渐渐坐满，替补席上有人不停活动脚踝。The coach waved the young player onto the field in the final minutes.
sceneCN: 这里是「运动员、球员」（第 1 个义项）；句意为教练在最后几分钟挥手让这名年轻球员上场。图中可辨识物件：替补席、边线、球鞋。

pos.zh: 运动员；播放器；演奏者；参与者

derivatives.zh: player 的基础动词，义为「玩；比赛；播放」
由 play 加形容词后缀 -ful 构成，义为「爱玩的；戏谑的」
由 play 与 off 复合而成，义为「附加赛；季后赛」

senses.title: Someone who plays a sport or game
senses.definition: a person who takes part in a sport or a game, especially as a profession
senses.definitionCN: 参加体育运动或比赛的人，尤指以此为职业者
senses.example: Their best player was injured in the first half.
senses.exampleCN: 他们最好的球员在上半场受伤了。
senses.why: The suffix -er simply marks the person who does the verb, so a player is first of all one who plays, whether on a field or at a table.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 只标示做这个动作的人，所以 player 首先是「玩的人」，无论在球场上还是在牌桌旁。

senses.title: A device that reproduces sound or video
senses.definition: a machine or program that plays recorded music, films or files
senses.definitionCN: 播放录音、影片或文件的机器或程序
senses.example: He put the disc into the player and turned up the volume.
senses.exampleCN: 他把光盘放进播放器，调高了音量。
senses.why: When machines took over the act of playing music, the same person-suffix was attached to the device, as if the machine now did the playing.
senses.whyCN: 当机器接手「播放音乐」这个动作时，同一个表人的后缀被安到了机器上，仿佛现在由机器来扮演这个角色。

senses.title: A musician
senses.definition: a person who plays a musical instrument
senses.definitionCN: 演奏乐器的人
senses.example: She is a fine player of the cello.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位出色的大提琴演奏者。
senses.why: Long before recordings, the one who played was a person with an instrument in hand, and this sense keeps the word close to the body and the fingers.
senses.whyCN: 在有录音之前，演奏的人就是手持乐器的人，这个义项让词始终贴近身体与手指。

senses.title: An active participant in a situation
senses.definition: a person or group that takes an active part in an activity, market or negotiation
senses.definitionCN: 积极介入某项活动、市场或谈判的人或团体
senses.example: The union is now a major player in the talks.
senses.exampleCN: 工会如今是谈判中的重要一方。
senses.why: From a game, the word widens to any contest of interests: whoever can make a move and change the outcome deserves to be called a player.
senses.whyCN: 从游戏出发，这个词扩展到任何利益博弈：谁能出手并改变结局，谁就配得上 player 这个称呼。

intro.en: Player is the plain English agent noun of play; the verb itself is old and its deeper origin is usually described as uncertain.
intro.cn: player 是 play 的英语施事名词，构词十分直接；动词 play 本身很古老，更早的来源一般被认为不确定。

items.en: The verb plegian meant to exercise, frolic or take part in a game.
items.cn: 动词 plegian 意为活动身体、嬉戏或参加游戏。

items.en: The related noun plega named a game, sport or quick movement.
items.cn: 相关名词 plega 指游戏、运动或轻快的动作。

items.en: Middle English play kept the sense of sport and amusement and began to cover music and performance.
items.cn: 中古英语 play 保留运动与娱乐义，并开始涵盖音乐与表演。

items.en: The native suffix -er, meaning one who does, made player out of play in the Middle English period.
items.cn: 本土后缀 -er 表示「做某事的人」，在中古英语时期把 play 变成了 player。

items.en: Modern English extends player to machines that reproduce sound and to anyone with a stake in a contest.
items.cn: 现代英语把 player 扩展到播放声音的机器，以及任何在一场较量中有份的人。

note.cn: 形近组收 play 词族，以及一个只是读音相近的词；近义组收表演、竞争或参与的人。

normalIntro.en: The word is play plus the person suffix, and every sense still asks the same question: who or what is doing the playing here?
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 play 加表人的后缀，每个义项都仍在问同一个问题：此刻是谁、是什么在「玩」？

normal.en: Player is play plus -er, the suffix for the one who does the action.
normal.cn: player 就是 play 加 -er，即「做这个动作的人」。

normal.en: A record player is a machine doing what a person used to do: playing the music.
normal.cn: 电唱机是一台机器在做过去由人做的事：播放音乐。

normal.en: A team player is not on the field but in the office: the image of a game is borrowed for cooperation.
normal.cn: team player 不在球场上而在办公室里：借用了比赛的画面来形容合作。

normal.en: Playful adds -ful, full of play, which shows how the family grows by short native suffixes.
normal.cn: playful 加 -ful，意为「充满玩的」，可见这个词族靠简短的本土后缀生长。

normal.en: Prayer is close in sound only; it comes from a Latin verb for begging and is not a relative.
normal.cn: prayer 只是读音相近，出自拉丁语中表示乞求的动词，并非同族词。

abstract.en: A word made by adding a person to an action reminds us that English often names a role before it names a thing.
abstract.cn: 给动作加上一个人，就造出一个词，这提醒人：英语常常先命名角色，再命名事物。

abstract.en: Calling a negotiator a player quietly turns a meeting into a game with moves and stakes.
abstract.cn: 把谈判者称作 player，悄悄把一场会议变成有招法、有输赢的游戏。

abstract.en: If a machine can be a player, then the word is less about being human than about taking the active part.
abstract.cn: 如果机器也能是 player，那么这个词的关键就不在于是不是人，而在于是否承担那个主动的角色。

examples.en: The old record player still works perfectly.

examples.en: She has become a key player in the peace talks.

definition_zh: 令人愉快的；和善的；合意的
definition_en: giving pleasure to the senses or the mind; also friendly in manner, or agreeable as an experience
core_image: 推开门的一瞬间，暖风、光线和淡淡香气一起涌上来，人不由自主放松了肩膀
scene: 午后的花园里风很轻，桌上刚切开的柠檬散出清香。The garden felt pleasant in the soft afternoon light.
sceneCN: 这里是「令人愉快的、宜人的」（第 1 个义项）；句意为在柔和的午后光线里，这座花园让人感到惬意。图中可辨识物件：柠檬、白桌布、树影。

pos.zh: 令人愉快的；和善的；合意的

derivatives.zh: pleasant 的同源动词，义为「使高兴；请」
由 please 加名词后缀 -ure 构成，义为「愉快；乐事」
由 pleasant 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「愉快地」
由否定前缀 un- 加 pleasant 构成，义为「令人不快的」

senses.title: Giving pleasure to the senses
senses.definition: giving a feeling of enjoyment to the senses, as a place, smell, sound or taste does
senses.definitionCN: 让感官产生愉悦，如地方、气味、声音或味道带来的舒服感
senses.example: The room was small but pleasant, with wide windows and warm light.
senses.exampleCN: 房间不大却很宜人，窗户宽大，光线温暖。
senses.why: The word began as the present participle of the verb to please, so anything pleasant is literally something that is pleasing you while you experience it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是动词 please 的现在分词，所以凡是 pleasant 的东西，字面上就是正在让你愉悦的东西。

senses.title: Friendly and agreeable in manner
senses.definition: kind, polite and easy to be with, said of a person or a person's manner
senses.definitionCN: 形容人或其举止亲切、有礼、好相处
senses.example: Our host gave us a pleasant smile and showed us to the table.
senses.exampleCN: 主人朝我们和善地一笑，把我们引到桌边。
senses.why: If a thing can please, a person can please too; the adjective then moves from the effect on the senses to the social warmth of someone's behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 既然事物能使人愉悦，人也能使人愉悦；于是这个形容词从感官效果转到某人举止带来的社交暖意。

senses.title: Agreeable to the mind
senses.definition: satisfying or welcome as a piece of news, a task or an arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 指消息、任务或安排令人满意、受欢迎
senses.example: It was a pleasant change to finish work before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 天没黑就干完活，这种改变让人舒心。
senses.why: Beyond the senses lies the mind: what fits our plans and leaves us easy is also called pleasant, which shows how far the pleasing image can reach.
senses.whyCN: 感官之外还有心智：合乎计划、让人安心的事也被称作 pleasant，可见「使人愉悦」这幅画面能延伸多远。

intro.en: Pleasant and please come from one Latin verb, but they entered English as different parts of speech: please as a verb, pleasant as its participle turned adjective.
intro.cn: pleasant 与 please 同出一个拉丁动词，但进入英语时词性不同：please 是动词，pleasant 是由它的分词转成的形容词。

items.en: The verb placere meant to please, to be agreeable, and it was used of things that satisfy a person.
items.cn: 动词 placere 意为使人高兴、令人满意，用来指让人称心的事物。

items.en: Its present participle placens, stem placent-, meant pleasing, the one giving pleasure.
items.cn: 它的现在分词 placens（词干 placent-）意为「令人愉悦的」，即正在带来愉悦的那一方。

items.en: Old French turned the participle into plaisant, an adjective meaning pleasing or charming.
items.cn: 古法语把这个分词变成形容词 plaisant，意为令人愉悦的、讨人喜欢的。

items.en: English borrowed plaisant as pleasant, keeping the adjective role, while the verb came in separately as please.
items.cn: 英语借入 plaisant 写作 pleasant，保留形容词身份；动词则另以 please 的形式进入。

items.en: Modern English uses pleasant for places, manners and news, and please for the act of giving pleasure or making a request.
items.cn: 现代英语用 pleasant 形容地方、举止与消息，用 please 表示使人高兴的动作或礼貌请求。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the please family and one word with a different origin; the near-meaning group gathers words for what delights or suits us.
note.cn: 形近组收 please 词族，以及一个来源不同的词；近义组收表示使人愉悦或合宜的词。

entries.definition: A feeling of enjoyment or satisfaction.

entries.definition: Giving pleasure, often of an experience.

entries.definition: Pleasant and easy to accept or be with.
entries.definitionCN: 令人愉快、容易相处或接受的。

entries.definition: Causing great pleasure.
entries.definitionCN: 带来很大快乐的。

entries.definition: Giving enjoyment, said of an activity.
entries.definitionCN: 令人享受的，多形容活动。

entries.definition: Pleasant or satisfactory in a general, everyday way.
entries.definitionCN: 日常口语中泛指令人愉快或满意的。

normalIntro.en: One Latin verb of pleasing produced both a verb and an adjective in English; keeping their parts of speech apart is the whole trick.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示「使人高兴」的拉丁动词在英语里同时产出了动词和形容词；分清两者的词性就是全部关键。

normal.en: Pleasant is the old participle of please: pleasing, therefore pleasant.
normal.cn: pleasant 是 please 古老的分词形式：正在使人愉悦的，因此是「令人愉快的」。

normal.en: Please is what you do; pleasant is what something is. The verb acts, the adjective describes.
normal.cn: please 是你做的动作；pleasant 是某物的性质。动词做事，形容词描述。

normal.en: Pleasure is the noun of the same family, formed with -ure, naming the feeling itself.
normal.cn: pleasure 是同族的动词名词，用 -ure 构成，指那种感觉本身。

normal.en: Pleasantly adds -ly to the adjective, turning it into the way something is done or felt.
normal.cn: pleasantly 在形容词后加 -ly，把它变成做某事或感受某事的方式。

normal.en: Plea looks similar but belongs to law and requests, not to pleasing.
normal.cn: plea 看着相近，却属于法律与请求的语义，与「愉悦」无关。

abstract.en: The same root gives a verb, an adjective and a noun, which shows how English lets one act spread across three roles.
abstract.cn: 同一个词根给出动词、形容词和名词，说明英语让一个动作分散到三种角色上。

abstract.en: A word that starts as an action becomes a quality: what pleases for long enough is simply pleasant.
abstract.cn: 一个从动作开始的词变成了性质：使人愉悦得够久，就干脆成了「令人愉快的」。

abstract.en: We call both air and manners pleasant, as if comfort in the body and comfort in company were the same feeling.
abstract.cn: 我们既说空气 pleasant，也说举止 pleasant，仿佛身体的舒适与相处时的舒适是同一种感受。

examples.en: We spent a pleasant afternoon by the river.
examples.cn: 我们在河边度过了一个愉快的下午。

examples.en: The staff were pleasant and quick to help.
examples.cn: 员工们态度和善，帮忙很及时。

examples.en: It was a pleasant surprise to see her at the door.
examples.cn: 在门口见到她，是个令人惊喜的意外。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普莱增特」——一进门就请（please）你坐下，气氛一下子变得舒服。

root: 拉丁语 placere（使人高兴）→ 现在分词 placens（词干 placent-）→ 古法语 plaisant → 英语 pleasant；同族的动词是 please。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the act of pleasing; the senses spread from the effect on the senses to the warmth of a person and to what suits the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「使人愉悦」这个动作；义项从对感官的作用，扩展到人的和善，再到合乎心意之事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door opens and warmth, light and a faint scent arrive together, so the shoulders loosen without being told.
core.cn: 核心意象：门一开，暖意、光线与淡淡香气一同涌来，肩膀不必吩咐就松了下来。

branches.en: a wide window and warm light in a small room
branches.cn: 小房间里一扇宽窗与温暖的光

branches.en: a host smiling and pointing to a chair
branches.cn: 主人微笑并示意一把椅子

branches.en: work finished before the sky goes dark
branches.cn: 天还没黑就干完了活

branches.en: comfort that comes from people and from timing
branches.cn: 来自人、也来自时机的舒适

branches.en: the same word for air, music and taste
branches.cn: 同一个词用于空气、音乐与味道

intro.en: A Latin verb of pleasing supplies the root, its participle ending supplies the shape, and French passes the adjective to English.
intro.cn: 一个表示「使人高兴」的拉丁动词提供词根，它的分词词尾提供外形，法语再把形容词传给英语。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 请；使高兴；使满意；随自己的意愿
definition_en: used as a courteous word when asking for something, or to give someone satisfaction
core_image: 菜单被轻轻推到你面前，对方退后半步，等你先开口
scene: 餐厅里，服务员把菜单轻轻推到你面前，退后一步等你点单。Please take your time; the waiter will come back in a moment.
sceneCN: 这里用的是「请」这一客套说法（第 1 个义项：礼貌地提出请求或邀请）；句意为请慢慢看，服务员稍后再过来。画面里有餐桌、菜单和退到一旁等候的服务员。

pos.zh: 使高兴；使满意；随自己的意愿

derivatives.zh: 由 please 加后缀 -ed 构成，表示「感到高兴的；满意的」
由 please 加后缀 -ing 构成，表示「令人愉快的；讨人喜欢的」
经古法语 plaisant 进入英语，与 please 同源，义为「令人愉快的；宜人的」
由否定前缀 dis- 加 please 构成，义为「使不快；惹恼」

senses.title: A courteous word in a request
senses.definition: used when asking for something or inviting someone to act, so that the request sounds polite
senses.definitionCN: 在提出请求或邀请别人做某事时使用，使语气显得客气
senses.example: Please close the window before you leave.
senses.exampleCN: 走之前请把窗户关好。
senses.why: The verb first meant to be agreeable to someone, and the request use keeps that attitude: the speaker puts the other person's comfort first and asks softly.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的动词本义是「令某人觉得合意」，请求用法延续的正是这种姿态：说话人先把对方的舒适放在前面，于是请求变得轻而客气。

senses.title: To give someone satisfaction
senses.definition: to make someone feel happy, content or satisfied
senses.definitionCN: 让某人感到高兴、满意或称心
senses.example: The simple answer seemed to please the whole committee.
senses.exampleCN: 这个简洁的答复似乎让整个委员会都很满意。
senses.why: Latin placere meant to be pleasing or acceptable to a person, so the one who is pleased is always the judge of whether the action worked.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 placere 意为「令人觉得合意、可接受」，所以被取悦的那个人始终是判断这件事成不成的人。

senses.title: To do as one wishes
senses.titleCN: 随自己的意愿；自行其便
senses.definition: to act according to your own wish rather than someone else's, as in the phrase please yourself
senses.definitionCN: 按自己的想法行事而不迁就别人，常见于 please yourself 这一说法
senses.example: You can please yourself about the seating arrangement.
senses.exampleCN: 座位怎么安排，你随自己的意思就好。
senses.why: If pleasing means making a person content, then pleasing oneself turns that contentment inward: the same verb now names a choice made for the speaker alone.
senses.whyCN: 既然 please 是「让人称心」，那么 please oneself 就是把这份称心转向自己：同一个动词在此指只为说话人自己作的选择。

intro.en: Please goes back to a Latin verb meaning to be agreeable, travelled through French, and in English shrank into the small polite word used in requests.
intro.cn: please 源自一个表示「令人觉得合意」的拉丁动词，经法语传入英语，最后又缩略成请求句里那个轻巧的客套词。

items.en: Placere meant to be pleasing or acceptable to someone, and it could describe a person as well as a thing.
items.cn: placere 意为令某人觉得愉快、可以接受，既可以形容事物，也可以形容人。

items.en: The related noun placitum named what seemed good and therefore a decision; it fed plea and plead rather than the verb please itself.
items.cn: 相关的名词 placitum 指「看起来好的事」，引申为决定；它后来生出 plea 与 plead，而不是动词 please 本身。

items.en: Old French used plaisir both as a verb meaning to please and as a noun for the pleasure that followed.
items.cn: 古法语中 plaisir 既是动词「使高兴」，也是名词「随之而来的快乐」。

items.en: Middle English plesen kept the verb and began to use it inside fixed courteous formulas.
items.cn: 中古英语的 plesen 保留了动词用法，并开始在固定的客套句式里使用它。

items.en: Modern English keeps please as a verb, splits off pleased and pleasant as adjectives, and uses the bare form as a courtesy marker.
items.cn: 现代英语让 please 继续作动词，分出 pleased 与 pleasant 两个形容词，又用光杆形式充当礼貌标记。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers relatives built on the Latin verb for being agreeable; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for satisfying someone.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「令人合意」这一动词上的同族词；近义组收表示「使满意」的动词。

entries.definition: Feeling happy or satisfied about something.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事感到高兴或满意的。

entries.definition: Enjoyable, agreeable or nice to be with.
entries.definitionCN: 令人愉快的；宜人的；好相处的。

entries.definition: To annoy or upset someone.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人不快；惹恼。

entries.definition: An urgent request, or the answer of an accused person in court.
entries.definitionCN: 恳求；被告在法庭上的答辩。

entries.definition: To give someone enough of what they want or need.
entries.definitionCN: 满足某人的需要或愿望。

entries.definition: To give someone great pleasure.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人极为高兴。

entries.definition: To please someone greatly, often by being attractive.
entries.definitionCN: 吸引并取悦某人。

entries.definition: To please someone by satisfying a wish or desire.
entries.definitionCN: 满足愿望而使某人高兴。

normalIntro.en: The family is built on one Latin verb for being agreeable, and its forms keep splitting into the feeling and the cause of the feeling.
normalIntro.cn: 这一族词建立在同一个表示「令人合意」的拉丁动词上，各个形式不断分成「感受」和「引起感受之物」两侧。

normal.en: Latin placere means to be agreeable to someone, so what pleases is what the other person accepts as good.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 placere 意为「令某人觉得合意」，所以能 please 人的东西，就是被对方认可为好而接受的东西。

normal.en: Please yourself puts the same agreement inside the speaker: the wish you agree with is your own.
normal.cn: please yourself 把这种「合意」转向说话人自己：你认同的愿望就是你自己的愿望。

normal.en: Pleased with -ed describes how a person feels; pleasing with -ing describes what produces that feeling.
normal.cn: 加了 -ed 的 pleased 说人心里怎么感觉；加了 -ing 的 pleasing 说是什么东西造成了这种感觉。

normal.en: Pleasant came through French, so it lost the s of please but kept the sense of being agreeable.
normal.cn: pleasant 经由法语而来，因此丢了 please 里的 s，却保留了「合意、讨人喜欢」的意思。

normal.en: The bare please in a request is the old verb worn down to a single polite signal.
normal.cn: 请求句里那个单独的 please，是老动词被磨成了一个纯粹的礼貌信号。

abstract.en: A word that means both make happy and if you would shows that politeness is a small gift of comfort.
abstract.cn: 一个词既能表示「使高兴」又能表示「请」，说明礼貌本身就是送给对方的一点舒适。

abstract.en: Every please hands the decision to the listener for a second, and that second is what makes the request gentle.
abstract.cn: 每一次说 please，都是把决定权交给听者一小会儿，而这一小会儿正是请求变得柔和的原因。

abstract.en: A pleased face, a pleasant evening and a polite request all sit under one root, because all three are about things being acceptable.
abstract.cn: 满意的脸色、宜人的夜晚、客气的请求同出一根，因为三者说的都是「合意」。

examples.en: Please leave your shoes at the door.
examples.cn: 请把鞋留在门口。

examples.en: The children were pleased with the new playground.
examples.cn: 孩子们对新游乐场很满意。

examples.en: She learned to please herself instead of chasing approval.
examples.cn: 她学会按自己的心意生活，而不是一味追求别人的认可。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑利兹」——把好处扑过去让对方得利，就是「使高兴」；开口求人先递一个「请」。

root: 拉丁语 placere（使愉快、被接受）经古法语 plaisir 进入英语；同族词多与「合意、愉快」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is being agreeable to someone; from it grow the courteous request, the act of giving satisfaction, and the choice to follow one's own wish.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「令某人觉得合意」；由此长出礼貌请求、使人满意这两种用法，以及按自己心意行事的选择。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a menu pushed gently forward while the other person steps back and waits.
core.cn: 核心意象：菜单被轻轻推到你面前，对方退后一步等你开口。

branches.en: a waiter stepping back so the guest can choose
branches.cn: 服务员退后一步，让客人自己挑选

branches.en: a child grinning at a new toy
branches.cn: 孩子对着新玩具咧嘴笑

branches.en: someone picking a seat without asking anyone
branches.cn: 有人不问别人就给自己挑了座位

branches.en: a host offering a second helping
branches.cn: 主人再添一勺，客人笑着接受

branches.en: a quiet evening that suits everyone
branches.cn: 一个人人满意的安静夜晚

intro.en: One Latin verb for being pleasing holds the family together, and two English suffixes split it into the feeling and the cause of the feeling.
intro.cn: 一个表示「令人愉快」的拉丁动词撑起这一族词，两个英语后缀再把它分成「感受」与「成因」两侧。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaningCN: 构成表示感受的形容词
构成表示成因的形容词

definition_zh: 愉快；快乐；乐事；消遣；荣幸
definition_en: a feeling of happiness or enjoyment, and also the thing or activity that produces it
core_image: 夏夜院子里，一把旧藤椅和一杯凉茶带来的松弛
scene: 忙完一整天，老人把藤椅搬到院子里坐下，长长舒了口气。The cool evening air gave her a quiet pleasure after a long day.
sceneCN: 这里指的是「愉快、快乐」这种心情（第 1 个义项）；句意为傍晚的凉风让劳累一天的她在心里松了下来。画面里有院子、藤椅和渐暗的天色。

pos.zh: 愉快；快乐；乐事；消遣；荣幸

derivatives.zh: 由 pleasure 加后缀 -able 构成，义为「令人愉快的」
由 pleasurable 加 -ly 构成，义为「愉快地」
由 pleasure 与 seeking 复合而成，义为「追求享乐的」

senses.title: A feeling of happiness
senses.definition: a feeling of happiness, enjoyment or satisfaction that comes from something agreeable
senses.definitionCN: 由合意之事带来的高兴、享受或满足的感受
senses.example: He listened to the rain with quiet pleasure.
senses.exampleCN: 他安静地听着雨声，心里很愉快。
senses.why: The noun comes from the same Latin verb as please, so it names the feeling that is left behind once something has been agreeable to you.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词与 please 同出拉丁语 placere（使愉快），因此它指的是某样东西合你心意之后，留在你心里的那份舒服。

senses.title: Something that gives enjoyment
senses.definition: an activity, event or object that gives you enjoyment and can be counted one by one
senses.definitionCN: 能带来愉快、可以一件件数出来的活动、事件或物件
senses.example: Her garden is her greatest pleasure.
senses.exampleCN: 她的花园是她最大的乐事。
senses.why: Once the feeling has a name, the countable thing that produces it borrows the same word, so a garden or a trip can itself be called a pleasure.
senses.whyCN: 心情先有了名字，接着产生这种心情的具体事物也沿用同一个词，于是一座花园、一趟旅行本身就能叫 pleasure。

senses.title: Enjoyment rather than work
senses.definition: enjoyment taken from an activity done for its own sake, not for duty or money
senses.definitionCN: 从只为本身而做的活动中得到的享受，不为职责或报酬
senses.example: He reads history for pleasure, not for exams.
senses.exampleCN: 他读历史是为了消遣，不是为了考试。
senses.why: Because the word already means enjoyment itself, adding the phrase for pleasure marks an activity as done only to obtain that enjoyment.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本身就指享受，所以 for pleasure 一出现，就等于声明这件事只为得到享受而做，不为别的。

senses.title: A courteous formula of willingness
senses.definition: used in polite formulas to say that you are glad to help or glad to have met someone
senses.definitionCN: 用于客套话，表示乐于帮忙或很高兴与某人相识
senses.example: It was a pleasure to work with such a careful team.
senses.exampleCN: 能和这样细致的团队共事是一件愉快的事。
senses.why: In social formulas the feeling is offered to the other person, so the word turns into a courteous way of saying that helping costs you nothing.
senses.whyCN: 在客套话里，这份愉快被送给对方，于是这个词变成一种礼貌表态：帮你这件事对我来说并不构成负担。

intro.en: Pleasure and please share one Latin source; the noun came into English through French and settled as the general word for enjoyment.
intro.cn: pleasure 与 please 共有一个拉丁源头；名词经法语进入英语，最后成为表示「享受」的通用词。

items.en: Placere meant to be pleasing or acceptable to someone, and its noun sense named the state of being agreeable.
items.cn: placere 意为令人愉快、可以接受，其名词用法指「合意」这个状态。

items.en: Old French used plaisir as a noun for enjoyment as well as a verb meaning to please.
items.cn: 古法语中 plaisir 既是名词「享受、快乐」，也是动词「使高兴」。

items.en: The Anglo-Norman form plesir carried the noun into legal and everyday English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 诺曼时期之后，盎格鲁-诺曼语形式 plesir 把这一名词带入英语的法律与日常用语。

items.en: Middle English pleasure covered both the feeling of enjoyment and the favour or consent shown to another person.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pleasure 既指享受的感受，也指给予别人的恩惠或同意。

items.en: Modern English keeps the general sense of enjoyment and adds fixed phrases for leisure, willing help and social courtesy.
items.cn: 现代英语保留「享受」这一总义，并固定出表示消遣、乐于相助与社交客套的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adjectives and relatives of the same Latin family; the near-meaning group gathers nouns for enjoyment.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词族里的形容词与同源词；近义组收表示「享受、快乐」的名词。

entries.definition: Enjoyable or nice, especially of a place, taste or manner.
entries.definitionCN: 令人愉快的；宜人的（多指地方、味道、态度）。

entries.definition: Giving pleasure, often of an experience.
entries.definitionCN: 带来愉快的，多形容体验。

entries.definition: Nice to look at or to experience.
entries.definitionCN: 好看的；令人满意的。

entries.definition: An old word for a pleasant place or a feeling of delight.
entries.definitionCN: 古语，指宜人之地或愉悦之感。

entries.definition: Great pleasure, stronger and more excited than ordinary enjoyment.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的快乐，比一般的享受更兴奋。

entries.definition: A feeling of deep happiness, often shown openly.
entries.definitionCN: 深深的喜悦，常外露。

entries.definition: The pleasure you get from doing or having something.
entries.definitionCN: 从做某事或拥有某物中得到的乐趣。

entries.definition: Satisfaction felt when a desire is met.
entries.definitionCN: 愿望得到满足时的快感。

entries.definition: Something special that gives pleasure.
entries.definitionCN: 让人开心的特别享受。

normalIntro.en: The noun is the please family seen from the inside: what started as being agreeable to someone becomes the enjoyment a person carries afterwards.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词是 please 词族从内侧看的样子：起初是「令某人合意」，后来变成人心里留下的那份享受。

normal.en: Pleasure and please share the Latin base placere, so a pleasure is what being pleased feels like from the inside.
normal.cn: pleasure 与 please 共用拉丁语基座 placere，所以 pleasure 就是「被取悦」从内部感受到的样子。

normal.en: Take pleasure in marks the source: the preposition points at whatever the enjoyment comes from.
normal.cn: take pleasure in 标出的是来源：介词指向让你得到享受的那件事。

normal.en: With pleasure answers a request, turning the enjoyment into willingness to help.
normal.cn: with pleasure 用来回应请求，把这份享受转成愿意帮忙的表态。

normal.en: For pleasure separates an activity from duty, which is why it appears with reading, travel and games.
normal.cn: for pleasure 把活动与职责分开，所以常和读书、旅行、游戏一起出现。

normal.en: The countable plural pleasures names the separate things that each give enjoyment, such as a meal or a visit.
normal.cn: 可数复数 pleasures 指一件件各自带来享受的具体事物，比如一顿饭、一次拜访。

abstract.en: The same root covers being agreeable, being pleased and giving pleasure, because enjoyment is a relation between a person and something else.
abstract.cn: 同一个词根覆盖「合意」「感到满意」「给予快乐」，因为享受本来就是人与某物之间的关系。

abstract.en: A pleasure is never purely inside: it always points back to the thing that caused it.
abstract.cn: 快乐从来不只在心里：它总是指回造成它的那个东西。

abstract.en: When the word becomes a formula of thanks, enjoyment turns into a small social gift.
abstract.cn: 当这个词变成道谢的套话，享受就转成了社交上的一点小礼物。

examples.en: He listened to the rain with quiet pleasure.
examples.cn: 他安静地听着雨声，心里很愉快。

examples.en: Her garden is her greatest pleasure.
examples.cn: 她的花园是她最大的乐事。

examples.en: It was a pleasure to work with such a careful team.
examples.cn: 能和这样细致的团队共事是一件愉快的事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑来酒」——朋友把好酒扑到你面前，喝下去浑身舒坦，那就是 pleasure。

root: 拉丁语 placere（使愉快）的名词用法经古法语 plaisir、盎格鲁-诺曼语 plesir 进入英语；与 please 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is inward enjoyment; the other senses add the countable source of joy, the leisure use and the courteous formula.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是心里的享受；其余义项分别添上可数的快乐来源、消遣用法与客套说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body sinking into a chair as the tension of the day drains away.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体陷进椅子，一天的紧绷慢慢退去。

branches.en: a long breath let out in a quiet courtyard
branches.cn: 在安静的院子里长舒一口气

branches.en: a garden the owner tends every morning
branches.cn: 主人每天清晨打理的园子

branches.en: a book read on a day off, with no deadline
branches.cn: 休息日不赶进度地读一本书

branches.en: a host saying it was no trouble at all
branches.cn: 主人说这完全不算麻烦

branches.en: a family meal that everyone lingers over
branches.cn: 一家人慢慢吃完的一顿饭

intro.en: The noun keeps the Latin verb for being agreeable, then adds a noun suffix and two English suffixes that build the adjectives around it.
intro.cn: 这个名词保留了表示「令人愉快」的拉丁动词，再靠一个名词后缀和两个英语后缀长出一圈形容词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: state or result of an action
items.meaningCN: 名词后缀：行为的状态或结果

definition_zh: 大量；许多；富足；足够地
definition_en: a large amount that is enough or more than enough, and informally an adverb meaning fully or very
core_image: 敞开的粮仓门，谷物堆成小山，多到不必去数
scene: 市集快散场时，果摊老板指着还剩大半的木箱，让你随便挑。There is plenty of time, so nobody needs to hurry.
sceneCN: 这里是「大量、许多」的用法（第 1 个义项），出现在 plenty of 这一结构中；句意为时间很充裕，谁都不必赶。画面里有快收摊的果摊、半箱水果和不再着急的顾客。

derivatives.zh: 由 plenty 的词干加 -eous 构成，文学用语，义为「丰盛的；大量的」
借拉丁 plenitudo 而来，与 plenty 同源，义为「丰足；充满」

senses.title: A large amount
senses.definition: a quantity that is large and usually more than is needed, used with of before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 数量很大、通常超出所需的量，放在名词前时用 of 连接
senses.example: There is plenty of room for everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 地方很宽裕，谁都坐得下。
senses.why: The noun descends from a Latin word for fullness, so plenty names a container that is already full rather than a measured number.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词源自拉丁语中表示「满」的词，所以 plenty 说的是一个已经装满的容器，而不是量出来的数字。

senses.title: A condition of abundance
senses.definition: a state or period in which there is a lot of something, especially food or money
senses.definitionCN: 某样东西尤其是食物或钱财很多的状况或时期
senses.example: The old stories describe years of plenty followed by years of hunger.
senses.exampleCN: 古老的故事里，富足的年份之后接着是饥饿的年份。
senses.why: Once the noun names a full supply, it can also name the whole period that enjoys such a supply, which is how a time of plenty appears.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个名词能指「装得满满的供给」，也就能指享有这种供给的整段时期，于是有了「富足的岁月」这种说法。

senses.title: Enough, or very
senses.definition: used informally as an adverb to mean enough or very, as in plenty hot
senses.definitionCN: 非正式地用作副词，表示「足够」或「很」，如 plenty hot
senses.example: The soup is plenty hot for me.
senses.exampleCN: 这汤对我来说已经够烫了。
senses.why: Because plenty already means more than enough, the same form can modify an adjective and say that the degree is fully sufficient.
senses.whyCN: 既然 plenty 本身就表示「超出所需」，同一个形式就能去修饰形容词，说明程度已经完全够了。

intro.en: Plenty came into English through French from a Latin word for fullness, and it stayed a noun while its relative plentiful became the adjective.
intro.cn: plenty 经法语从表示「满」的拉丁词进入英语，一直保持名词身份，而它的同族词 plentiful 则成了形容词。

items.en: Plenus meant full, and it supplied the whole family of English words about abundance.
items.cn: plenus 意为「满的」，为英语里一整族表示「充足」的词提供了来源。

items.en: The noun plenitas meant fullness or completeness, the abstract state of being full.
items.cn: 名词 plenitas 意为「满、完备」，指装满这一抽象状态。

items.en: Old French plente kept the sense of abundance and was used of harvests, stores and wealth.
items.cn: 古法语 plente 保留了「充足」之义，用于收成、储备与财富。

items.en: Middle English borrowed plente as a noun and used it in phrases about food, money and time.
items.cn: 中古英语把 plente 借作名词，用于谈论食物、钱财与时间的词组。

items.en: Modern English fixed the spelling plenty and added the informal adverbial use, as in plenty hot.
items.cn: 现代英语把拼写固定为 plenty，并添上非正式的副词用法，如 plenty hot。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin full family around the noun; the near-meaning group gathers nouns for a large quantity.
note.cn: 形近组收围绕这个名词的拉丁语「满」词族；近义组收表示「大量」的名词。

entries.definition: The adjective formed from this noun with -ful.
entries.definitionCN: 由这个名词加 -ful 构成的形容词。

entries.definition: An older adjective meaning abundant.
entries.definitionCN: 较老的形容词，义为「丰盛的」。

entries.definition: A formal noun for fullness or completeness.
entries.definitionCN: 正式用语，指满盈、完备。

entries.definition: Full or complete, as of a session with everyone present.
entries.definitionCN: 完全的；全体出席的。

entries.definition: A very large quantity of something.
entries.definitionCN: 极大量的某物。

entries.definition: A large amount, as in a lot of time.
entries.definitionCN: 大量，如 a lot of time。

entries.definition: A large amount of something good, as in a wealth of detail.
entries.definitionCN: 大量美好的事物，如 a wealth of detail。

entries.definition: An extremely large supply of something.
entries.definitionCN: 极其丰富的供给。

normalIntro.en: The noun is the Latin idea of fullness standing on its own, before any suffix turns it into an adjective.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词就是拉丁语「满」这一概念独立站着的样子，还没被任何后缀变成形容词。

normal.en: Plenty is the bare noun of fullness, so it needs of before another noun: plenty of time, plenty of room.
normal.cn: plenty 是表示「满」的光杆名词，所以接另一个名词时要加 of：plenty of time、plenty of room。

normal.en: Plentiful adds -ful to the same noun, which is why the adjective and the noun look so alike.
normal.cn: plentiful 是在同一个名词后加 -ful，所以形容词与名词长得几乎一样。

normal.en: Years of plenty is the noun naming a whole period, not a single heap of goods.
normal.cn: years of plenty 是名词在指一整段时期，而不是一堆货物。

normal.en: In plenty drops the of and works as an adverbial phrase meaning in large amounts.
normal.cn: in plenty 去掉 of，作副词性短语，表示「大量地」。

normal.en: The informal adverb use, as in plenty hot, keeps the meaning enough while changing the word class.
normal.cn: plenty hot 这类非正式副词用法保留了「足够」的意思，只改变了词性。

abstract.en: A noun for fullness can describe a season, a table or a stretch of time, because abundance is always abundance of something.
abstract.cn: 表示「满」的名词能形容一季、一桌或一段时间，因为充足总是某样东西的充足。

abstract.en: Plenty does not measure; it says that counting is no longer necessary.
abstract.cn: plenty 不做计量，它说的是「已经不必再数了」。

abstract.en: The same root gives a noun for stores and an adjective for harvests, so grammar follows the difference between the heap and its quality.
abstract.cn: 同一个词根给出指库存的名词和指收成的形容词，语法正好对应「堆」与「性质」的差别。

examples.en: There is plenty of room for everyone.
examples.cn: 地方很宽裕，谁都坐得下。

examples.en: The old stories describe years of plenty followed by years of hunger.
examples.cn: 古老的故事里，富足的年份之后接着是饥饿的年份。

examples.en: The soup is plenty hot for me.
examples.cn: 这汤对我来说已经够烫了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑棱提」——粮食扑棱棱堆满仓，提到手软也提不完，就是 plenty。

root: 拉丁语 plenus（满的）→ plenitas（充足）→ 古法语 plente → 中古英语 plente → 现代英语 plenty。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a full supply; the noun then extends to a whole period of abundance, and the same form works informally as an adverb of degree.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「装得满满的供给」；名词由此扩展到整段富足时期，同一形式又非正式地充当程度副词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: barn doors open on grain piled into a small hill, too much to bother counting.
core.cn: 核心意象：粮仓门敞着，谷物堆成小山，多到懒得去数。

branches.en: a jar filled well above the recipe
branches.cn: 罐子装得远超配方所需

branches.en: a village eating well for a whole season
branches.cn: 全村整整一季吃得宽裕

branches.en: a coat warm enough without a scarf
branches.cn: 外套够暖，不必再围围巾

branches.en: a table with more dishes than guests
branches.cn: 菜比客人还多的一桌

branches.en: store rooms that stay full through winter
branches.cn: 整个冬天都满着的库房

intro.en: The noun keeps the Latin stem of fullness, and English adds a noun suffix plus two later relatives built on the same stem.
intro.cn: 这个名词保留了拉丁语表示「满」的词干，英语再加上一个名词后缀，以及两个由同一词干长出的同族词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 情节；小块土地；密谋；绘制；标出
definition_en: the arranged sequence of events in a story; a small measured piece of land; a secret plan made by a group; and to mark a course or a set of data on a map or graph
core_image: 田埂围出一小块地，旁边有人低头在纸上描出一条曲线
scene: 剧本读到一半，作者在页边画出一个方框，把人物下一步的动作圈了进去。She sketched the plot of her next novel on the back of an envelope.
sceneCN: 这里 plot 是「情节」（第 1 个义项：故事中事件的安排）；句意为她在信封背面勾勒出下一部小说的情节。图中可辨识物件：剧本、页边方框、信封。

derivatives.zh: 由 plot 双写末尾的 t 加表示「人或工具」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「密谋者；绘图仪」
由 plot 加 -ing 构成，义为「密谋；绘图」
由前缀 sub-（在下、次要）加 plot 构成，义为「次要情节」

senses.title: The sequence of events in a story
senses.definition: the organized sequence of events and actions that makes up a story, play or film
senses.definitionCN: 构成小说、戏剧或电影的故事事件与行动的有序安排
senses.example: The plot turns on a letter that never arrives.
senses.exampleCN: 情节的关键是一封始终没有送达的信。
senses.why: Plot first named a piece of ground marked off by boundaries, and a story line is likewise a stretch staked out by the writer: a beginning, a turn and an end. The sense is recorded from the seventeenth century, when critics needed a word for the arrangement of incidents in a play.
senses.whyCN: plot 最初指用界线围出的一块地，而故事线同样是一段由作者圈定的范围：开端、转折与结局。这个义项在十七世纪有记录，当时评论家需要一个词来指戏剧中事件的安排。

senses.title: A small measured piece of land
senses.definition: a small area of ground marked out for a particular use, such as building a house or growing vegetables
senses.definitionCN: 为特定用途（如盖房或种菜）而划出的一小块土地
senses.example: They grow beans on a narrow plot behind the house.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在屋后一小块窄地上种豆子。
senses.why: This is the oldest recorded sense: Old English plot named a definite piece of ground, most likely because the patch had been marked off from the rest. The measuring of land by lines is still visible in a garden plot or a building plot.
senses.whyCN: 这是有记录的最古老义项：古英语 plot 指一块界限明确的地，很可能因为这片地被从周围划了出来。用线划分土地的动作至今仍看得见，比如菜地或建筑用地。

senses.title: A secret plan made by several people
senses.definition: a secret plan by a group to do something harmful or unlawful
senses.definitionCN: 一群人暗中策划做有害或违法之事的计划
senses.example: The police uncovered a plot to rob the bank.
senses.exampleCN: 警方破获了一起抢劫银行的阴谋。
senses.why: English speakers blended the native land word with Old French complot, a group scheme; the two forms merged in sound and meaning, so the idea of a secret scheme attached itself to plot and has stayed ever since.
senses.whyCN: 说英语的人把本土表示土地的那个词与古法语 complot（一伙人的图谋）混同，两个形式在读音和意义上合流，于是「暗中图谋」的意思就附着在 plot 上，一直留到今天。

senses.title: To mark a course or data on a graph
senses.definition: to mark points, a line or a course on a map or graph, or to follow and record a moving path
senses.definitionCN: 在地图或图表上标出点、线或路线，或跟踪记录一条移动的轨迹
senses.example: The software plots the temperature against the hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这个软件把温度随时间的变化绘成曲线。
senses.why: Marking points on a sheet repeats on paper the old act of marking ground. Sailors plotted a course by laying it out point by point, and the same verb now covers data points drawn on a graph.
senses.whyCN: 在纸上标出各个点，等于把当年在土地上做记号的动作重做一遍。水手靠逐点标出来绘制航线，同一个动词如今也用于把数据点画成图表。

intro.en: Plot is an old English word for a piece of ground whose earlier origin is uncertain; the sense of a secret scheme came from French complot, and the story sense grew out of the marked-out ground.
intro.cn: plot 是英语中表示一块土地的古老词，更早的来源不确定；「阴谋」的意思来自法语 complot，而「情节」的意思则从划出来的那块地引申而来。

items.en: Old English plot named a definite piece of ground, and its earlier origin is uncertain; it may have meant a patch marked off from the rest.
items.cn: 古英语 plot 指一块界限明确的地，更早的来源不确定，可能指从周围划出来的一小片。

items.en: Middle English used plot for a small field or a measured patch, and the word stayed close to land and boundaries.
items.cn: 中古英语用 plot 指小田地或量好的一小块地，词义始终离不开土地与界线。

items.en: Old French complot meant a group scheme or conspiracy; English speakers heard it as the same word as plot and merged the two meanings.
items.cn: 古法语 complot 指一伙人的图谋或阴谋；说英语的人把它听成与 plot 同一个词，两种意思便合在一起。

items.en: In the sixteenth century plot could mean a secret plan, and by the seventeenth critics used it for the arranged incidents of a play.
items.cn: 十六世纪时 plot 已可指秘密计划，到十七世纪评论家又用它指戏剧中安排好的事件。

items.en: Modern English keeps the land, the scheme and the story, and adds the verb of charting a course or plotting data.
items.cn: 现代英语保留土地、阴谋与故事三层意思，又加上绘制航线或标绘数据的动词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers this word's own family plus the French cousin behind the conspiratorial sense; the near-meaning group gathers words for a story line, a scheme and a patch of ground.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词自己的词族，以及带来「阴谋」义的那个法语近亲；近义组收表示故事线、图谋与小块地的词。

entries.definition: An old word for a group conspiracy, borrowed from French and now almost out of use.
entries.definitionCN: 指一伙人阴谋的旧词，借自法语，如今几乎不再使用。

entries.definition: A person who makes a secret plan, or a machine that draws graphs.
entries.definitionCN: 密谋的人，或绘制图表的机器；绘图仪。

entries.definition: A secondary story line running beside the main one.
entries.definitionCN: 与主线并行的一条次要情节。

entries.definition: The main sequence of events in a story, seen as a line.
entries.definitionCN: 故事中主要事件的走向，被看作一条线。

entries.definition: The main line of events in a story.
entries.definitionCN: 故事中事件的主线。

entries.definition: A plan, often a secret or a clever one.
entries.definitionCN: 计划，常指秘密或巧妙的安排。

entries.definition: A small piece of ground, especially one used for growing something.
entries.definitionCN: 一小块土地，尤指用来种东西的。

entries.definition: A secret plan by several people to do something wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 数人暗中策划做坏事的图谋。

normalIntro.en: The word began as ground marked off by lines, and that single picture of a bounded patch keeps reappearing: a patch of soil, a stretch of events, a set of points on a sheet.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从被线条划出的土地开始，而「一块有边界的范围」这个画面反复出现：一块土、一段事件、纸上一组点。

normal.en: Old English plot meant a measured piece of ground, so the garden plot and the building plot are the oldest uses of the word.
normal.cn: 古英语 plot 指量好的一块地，所以菜地与建筑用地是这个词最古老的用法。

normal.en: A story plot is a stretch of events with a boundary: the writer decides where the tale starts and where it stops.
normal.cn: 故事的情节是一段有边界的事件：作者决定故事从哪里开始、到哪里结束。

normal.en: The conspiratorial sense came from French complot, which English speakers heard as the same word and merged with plot.
normal.cn: 阴谋义来自法语 complot，说英语的人把它听成同一个词，于是与 plot 合并。

normal.en: To plot a graph is to mark points one by one, the way a surveyor marks a patch of ground.
normal.cn: plot 一张图就是逐个标出点，正如测量员标出一块地。

normal.en: Subplot adds sub-, meaning under or secondary, so it names a story line running beneath the main one.
normal.cn: subplot 加了表示「在下、次要」的 sub-，指主线之下的一条情节。

abstract.en: A plot is a line drawn around a piece of the world so that attention can settle there.
abstract.cn: 情节是围绕世界的一小块画出的线，好让注意力落在那里。

abstract.en: The same word holds a garden and a conspiracy, because both are marked out in advance by someone who intends to use them.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既装着菜地也装着阴谋，因为两者都是有人事先划出来、打算加以利用的。

abstract.en: On a graph, a plot is a promise that a movement can be turned into a shape.
abstract.cn: 在图表上，一条绘出的曲线是一个承诺：一段运动可以被变成形状。

examples.en: The plot turns on a letter that never arrives.
examples.cn: 情节的关键是一封始终没有送达的信。

examples.en: They grow beans on a narrow plot behind the house.
examples.cn: 他们在屋后一小块窄地上种豆子。

examples.en: The software plots the temperature against the hour.
examples.cn: 这个软件把温度随时间的变化绘成曲线。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑络」——线索一条条扑上来，又络在一起，故事就有了情节；记住 plot 是情节，也是小块地。

root: 古英语 plot 指一块划定的土地，更早来源不确定；表示「阴谋」的意思受古法语 complot 影响而合流；表示「情节」的意思在十七世纪从「划出的一段范围」引申出来。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a bounded patch; the senses run from a measured piece of land, to a stretch of events marked out by a writer, to a scheme hatched in secret, and finally to points marked on a sheet.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一块有边界的范围；义项从量好的土地，走到作者划出的一段事件，再到暗中策划的图谋，最后落到纸上标出的点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small field fenced by ridges, and a hand tracing a curve beside it on paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：田埂围出的一小块地，旁边有人在纸上描出一条曲线。

branches.cn: 一串事件因一封信而转向

intro.cn: 这个词是来源不确定的英语本土名词，词族靠前缀与后缀扩展，而「阴谋」义则倚靠一个法语近亲。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for the land sense, whose origin is uncertain; the conspiracy sense came through French from a form whose own source is also disputed.
latinIntro.cn: 表示土地的这个义项没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，来源不确定；阴谋义经法语传入，其来源同样有争议。

items.meaning: one who plots, or a drawing machine

definition_zh: 插头；塞子；插上电源；堵塞；插入
definition_en: a small device with metal pins that connects a wire to an electrical socket; a piece of material that blocks a hole; to connect an appliance to power or push something firmly in; and to block an opening or a gap
core_image: 一只手把橡胶塞按进瓶口，另一只手把插头推向插座
scene: 浴缸里的水一直往下漏，修理工蹲下来查看排水口。He pulled the plug out of the bath and watched the water drain away.
sceneCN: 这里 plug 是「塞子」（第 2 个义项：堵住孔洞的东西）；句意为他拔掉浴缸的塞子，看着水流走。图中可辨识物件：浴缸、排水口、橡胶塞。

derivatives.zh: 由否定前缀 un- 加 plug 构成，义为「拔掉插头；断开电源」
由 plug 双写末尾的 g 加 -er 构成，义为「塞东西的人；埋头苦干的人」
由动词短语 plug in 加连字符凝固而成，义为「插件；插入式装置」

senses.title: An electrical connector with metal pins
senses.definition: a small device with metal pins that joins a wire or an appliance to an electrical socket
senses.definitionCN: 带金属插脚的小装置，把电线或电器接到电源插座上
senses.example: The plug does not fit this socket.
senses.exampleCN: 这个插头跟这个插座不配套。
senses.why: The electrical sense is a later use of the older stopper: the plug is pushed into a socket exactly as a bung is pushed into a hole, and it is the tight fit that carries the current.
senses.whyCN: 插头这个义项是较晚从「塞子」引申出来的：插头被推进插座，正像塞子被推进孔里，正是这种严丝合缝的嵌入把电流接通。

senses.title: A piece of material that blocks a hole
senses.definition: a piece of rubber, wood or cork used to close a hole, especially in a bath, sink or barrel
senses.definitionCN: 用来堵住孔洞的橡胶、木头或软木块，尤指浴缸、水槽或桶上的
senses.example: He pulled the plug out of the bath and watched the water drain away.
senses.exampleCN: 他拔掉浴缸的塞子，看着水流走。
senses.why: This is the earliest English sense, taken from Dutch: a shaped piece forced into an opening so that nothing passes. Every later use of the word is a version of that tight fit.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语里最早的义项，借自荷兰语：一块成形的东西被硬塞进开口，让任何东西都过不去。这个词后来的用法，都是这种「嵌紧」的变体。

senses.title: To push in or connect to power
senses.definition: to push something firmly into an opening, or to connect an appliance to electricity by means of a plug
senses.definitionCN: 把某物用力推进开口，或通过插头把电器接通电源
senses.example: She plugged the heater into the wall and turned it on.
senses.exampleCN: 她把取暖器插到墙上，然后打开。
senses.why: The verb performs the noun: to plug is to behave like a plug, driving a shaped end into a matching hole until it holds. Electricity turned that motion into the everyday way of giving a machine power.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词的动作做出来：plug 一样东西，就是像塞子那样把成形的末端推进相配的孔，直到卡住。电的出现让这个动作成了给机器供电的日常方式。

senses.title: To block an opening or a gap
senses.definition: to fill a hole, a leak or a gap so that nothing can pass through it
senses.definitionCN: 把孔洞、漏洞或缺口填住，使任何东西都无法通过
senses.example: They plugged the leak with a strip of cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用一条布堵住了漏水处。
senses.why: A plug stops flow by occupying the opening, so the verb extends from forcing in a stopper to any act of filling a gap, including plugging a hole in a budget or in an argument.
senses.whyCN: 塞子靠占住开口来阻断流动，所以动词从「塞入塞子」扩展到任何填补缺口的动作，包括补上预算或论证里的漏洞。

intro.en: Plug is a Germanic borrowing from Middle Dutch, where it named a block or a bung; its deeper origin is uncertain, and English first used it for a stopper before it named an electrical connector.
intro.cn: plug 是从中古荷兰语借来的日耳曼词，原指木块或桶塞；更早的来源不确定，英语先用它指塞子，后来才指电插头。

items.en: Middle Dutch plugge named a block or a bung, a shaped piece used to stop a hole; the deeper origin of the form is uncertain.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 plugge 指木块或桶塞，即用来堵孔的成形木块；这个形式更早的来源不确定。

items.en: English borrowed plug in the seventeenth century for a stopper in a barrel, a bath or a pipe.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 plug，指桶、浴缸或管道里的塞子。

items.en: The word widened to any blocking piece, and the verb appeared for stopping a hole or a leak.
items.cn: 词义扩展到任何起堵塞作用的东西，动词也出现了，表示堵住孔洞或漏洞。

items.en: When wires needed joints, the shaped metal connector that fitted into a socket was called a plug, by analogy with a bung.
items.cn: 当电线需要接头时，那种嵌进插座的成形金属连接件被叫作 plug，这是类比桶塞而来的。

items.en: Modern English adds plug in, unplug and the informal sense of promoting something by repeating its name.
items.cn: 现代英语又加上 plug in、unplug，以及反复提名字来宣传某物的口语义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the word's own derivatives and compounds; the near-meaning group gathers objects and verbs for stopping or joining a hole.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词自己的派生词与复合词；近义组收堵孔、接孔一类的物件与动词。

entries.definition: To disconnect an appliance by pulling out its plug.
entries.definitionCN: 拔掉插头，使电器断电。

entries.definition: A person who plugs something, or who works steadily at a task.
entries.definitionCN: 塞东西的人，或埋头苦干的人。

entries.definition: A small module or program that is connected into a larger system.
entries.definitionCN: 接入更大系统的小模块或程序；插件。

entries.definition: The hole in a bath or sink that a plug closes.
entries.definitionCN: 浴缸或水槽里由塞子堵住的排水孔。

entries.definition: An object pushed into the neck of a bottle to close it.
entries.definitionCN: 塞进瓶口使其封闭的物件。

entries.definition: A round piece of wood or rubber that closes the hole of a barrel.
entries.definitionCN: 封住桶口的圆形木塞或橡胶塞。

entries.definition: The fitting in a wall that receives a plug.
entries.definitionCN: 墙上承接插头的插座。

entries.definition: To stop something passing through an opening.
entries.definitionCN: 阻止某物通过开口；堵塞。

normalIntro.en: The word arrived from Dutch as a shaped stopper, and the whole family keeps the picture of something pressed tightly into a hole.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从荷兰语进来时就是一块成形的塞子，整个词族都带着「紧紧压进孔里」的画面。

normal.en: Middle Dutch plugge meant a block or a bung, so the bath plug is closer to the original sense than the electrical plug.
normal.cn: 中古荷兰语 plugge 意为木块或桶塞，所以浴缸塞子比电插头更接近本义。

normal.en: The electrical plug is named by analogy: metal pins are pressed into a socket the way a bung is pressed into a barrel.
normal.cn: 电插头是类比得名：金属插脚被压进插座，正如桶塞被压进桶口。

normal.en: Unplug adds the reversing prefix un- and means to take the plug out, cutting the current.
normal.cn: unplug 加了表示相反动作的前缀 un-，意为拔出插头、切断电流。

normal.en: Plug the gap keeps the old physical idea: something is put into an opening so that nothing slips through.
normal.cn: plug the gap 保留了古老的实物想法：把东西放进缺口，让任何东西都漏不过去。

normal.en: Plug-in is written with a hyphen as a noun, and the same two words without a hyphen form the verb phrase plug in.
normal.cn: plug-in 作名词时带连字符；同样两个词不带连字符时则是动词短语 plug in。

abstract.en: A plug is a small object whose whole purpose is to be exactly the wrong shape for the hole it fills.
abstract.cn: 塞子的全部用处，就是恰好以不合适的形状占满它填的孔。

abstract.en: Electricity turned a bung into a bridge: the same tight fit now carries power instead of stopping water.
abstract.cn: 电把桶塞变成了桥：同样的紧密嵌合，如今输送电力而不是拦住水。

abstract.en: To plug a gap is to admit that a system has a hole and to decide it must not be seen.
abstract.cn: 填补缺口，就是承认系统有个洞，并决定不让它被看见。

examples.en: The plug does not fit this socket.
examples.cn: 这个插头跟这个插座不配套。

examples.en: He pulled the plug out of the bath and watched the water drain away.
examples.cn: 他拔掉浴缸的塞子，看着水流走。

examples.en: They plugged the leak with a strip of cloth.
examples.cn: 他们用一条布堵住了漏水处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「噗嗤」——塞子塞进瓶口发出噗嗤一声；记住 plug 是塞子，也是插头。

root: 中古荷兰语 plugge（木块、桶塞）借入英语为 plug，更早来源不确定：先指塞子，十九世纪后类比桶塞，指嵌入插座的金属插头，再引申出插入、堵塞等动词义。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a shaped piece pressed into an opening; the senses run from the stopper, to the electrical connector that copies it, to the act of connecting, and finally to the act of blocking a gap.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一块被压进开口的成形物件；义项从塞子，走到模仿它的电插头，再到接通电源的动作，最后落到堵住缺口的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rubber bung forced into a bottle mouth, and a hand pushing a plug toward a socket.
core.cn: 核心意象：橡胶塞被按进瓶口，另一只手把插头推向插座。
