branches.cn: 插头推进墙上插座

branches.en: a rubber bung in a bath drain
branches.cn: 浴缸排水口里的橡胶塞

branches.en: a heater coming alive at the wall
branches.cn: 取暖器在插座上亮起

branches.en: a cloth stuffed into a leaking pipe
branches.cn: 布团塞进漏水的管子

branches.en: a gap in a budget being filled
branches.cn: 预算缺口被补上

intro.en: The word is a Dutch borrowing of a stopper, and English builds its family with a reversing prefix, an agent suffix and compounds made from the verb phrase.
intro.cn: 这个词是借自荷兰语的「塞子」，英语用表示相反动作的前缀、表示施动者的后缀，以及由动词短语凝固成的复合词来扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; it came into English from Middle Dutch, and the further origin of the Dutch noun is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它从中古荷兰语进入英语，而那个荷兰语名词更早的来源不确定。

items.meaning: a module connected into a system

definition_zh: 加；加上；再加；正的；有利的；优势
definition_en: used between two amounts to show addition; added on top of what is already there; greater than zero or favourable; and an advantage that counts in someone's favour
core_image: 算板上一颗石子被推到另一颗旁边，两堆并成一堆
scene: 账单摊在桌子中央，服务员把最后一道菜名也添在末尾。The bill came to forty pounds, plus a small service charge.
sceneCN: 这里 plus 是「加、加上」（第 1 个义项：在原有数量之外再添一份）；句意为一共四十英镑，外加一点服务费。图中可辨识物件：账单、笔、餐盘。

collocations.zh: 好处在于；从有利的一面看

derivatives.zh: 由前缀 sur-（超过）加拉丁语 plus（更多）构成，义为「剩余；盈余」
与 plus 同出拉丁语表示「更多」的词干 plures，义为「复数的；多数的」
由 plural 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「多数；相对多数票」

senses.title: Added to an amount
senses.definition: used between two numbers or amounts to show that the second is added to the first
senses.definitionCN: 放在两个数字或数量之间，表示把后者加到前者之上
senses.example: Two plus three makes five.
senses.exampleCN: 二加三等于五。
senses.why: Latin plus meant more, and arithmetic borrowed the word to stand at the exact point where one quantity becomes more by taking in another.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 plus 意为「更多」，算术把这个词放在一个数量因并入另一个而变多的那个位置上。

senses.title: In addition to what is mentioned
senses.definition: used after a statement to add something further that is also included
senses.definitionCN: 在一句话之后补充还有某项东西也算在内
senses.example: The room has a balcony, plus a view of the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间带阳台，另外还能看到港口。
senses.why: If plus can add one number to another, it can also add one fact to another, so the word moves from counting to piling extra items onto a statement.
senses.whyCN: 既然 plus 能把一个数加到另一个数上，也就能把一件事加进另一句话，于是这个词从算数走到了在陈述上追加条件。

senses.title: Above zero or favourable
senses.definition: greater than zero, or working in one's favour rather than against it
senses.definitionCN: 大于零的，或对人有利而不是不利的
senses.example: A plus factor is that the school is within walking distance.
senses.exampleCN: 一个有利因素是学校走几步就到。
senses.why: On a scale with zero in the middle, whatever falls on the higher side is marked with a plus, and from that mark the word comes to mean anything that counts for you.
senses.whyCN: 在以零为中点的刻度上，落在较高一侧的都标上加号，从这个记号起，这个词就用来指任何对你有利的东西。

senses.title: An advantage
senses.definition: a quality or circumstance that gives someone an advantage
senses.definitionCN: 能让人占上风的某种长处或条件
senses.example: Speaking two languages is a real plus in this job.
senses.exampleCN: 会两种语言在这份工作里是真正的优势。
senses.why: Once a plus marks what lies on the good side of zero, the mark itself becomes a noun for the good thing it stands for, which is why a strength is simply called a plus.
senses.whyCN: 当加号用来标出零以上的那一侧，这个记号本身就变成了名词，指它所代表的好处，所以一项长处直接被叫作 a plus。

intro.en: Plus is a Latin comparative meaning more, and English took it over unchanged for arithmetic before widening it to extra items, positive values and personal advantages.
intro.cn: plus 是拉丁语中表示「更多」的比较级形式，英语原样借来用于算术，随后扩展到额外的项目、正值与个人优势。

items.en: Plus meant more, and Roman writers used it in phrases of addition and comparison long before any symbol existed.
items.cn: plus 意为更多，早在任何符号出现之前，罗马作家就用它来表示添加与比较。

items.en: The stem behind plus is plures, more or several, which also gave the adjective pluralis and English plural.
items.cn: plus 背后的词干是 plures，意为更多、数个，它同时给出了形容词 pluralis 与英语的 plural。

items.en: English borrowed plus in arithmetic and surveying, where it named the operation of adding rather than a written sign.
items.cn: 英语在十六、十七世纪把 plus 借入算术与测量，当时它指添加这个运算，而不是一个写出来的符号。

items.en: The cross-shaped mark for addition was read aloud as plus, so the sign and the word became inseparable in schoolroom practice.
items.cn: 表示相加的十字形记号被读作 plus，符号与词在课堂练习里从此分不开。

items.en: Modern English uses plus for extra items, for positive numbers and results, and, as a noun, for any advantage a person or plan holds.
items.cn: 现代英语用 plus 表示额外项目、正值与好结果，并作名词指人或方案拥有的任何优势。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem for more and adds two words that merely share letters; the near-meaning group gathers words for addition and for an extra benefit.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁语表示「更多」的词干展开，另收两个只是字母相像的词；近义组收表示添加与额外好处的词。

entries.definition: An amount left over after what is needed has been used; it joins sur-, over, to the Latin stem of plus.
entries.definitionCN: 需要之外剩下的数量；由表示「超过」的 sur- 加 plus 的拉丁词干构成。

entries.definition: The form of a word used for more than one thing; it comes from the same Latin stem plures.
entries.definitionCN: 用于表示多于一个事物的词形；来自同一个拉丁词干 plures。

entries.definition: A thick soft fabric, or a word for something luxurious; it looks like plus but comes from a different French source.
entries.definitionCN: 厚而柔软的织物，也形容奢华；拼写与 plus 相近，却来自另一个法语来源，词源不同。

entries.definition: A soft round fruit with a stone; the resemblance is spelling only, since the fruit name has another origin.
entries.definitionCN: 一种带核的柔软圆果；只是拼写相像，这个水果名另有来源。

entries.definition: The act of adding something, or the thing that is added.
entries.definitionCN: 添加的行为，或被添加上去的东西。

entries.definition: An extra amount given beyond what is usual or expected.
entries.definitionCN: 在通常或预期之外额外给出的东西。

entries.definition: Something that puts a person in a better position than others.
entries.definitionCN: 使人比他人处于更有利地位的东西。

entries.definition: More than the usual or expected amount, or something added.
entries.definitionCN: 多于通常或预期的，或额外添加的东西。

normalIntro.en: One Latin comparative, more, supplies the whole family: the arithmetic word, the leftover noun, the plural form and the noun for an advantage.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拉丁语比较级「更多」撑起整族词：算术里的加、剩下的名词、复数形式，以及表示优势的名词。

normal.en: Latin plus means more, so the word sits exactly where a quantity grows by taking in another.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 plus 意为更多，所以这个词正待在一个数量因并入另一个而变多的位置上。

normal.en: Surplus is sur-, over, plus the same stem: the amount that goes beyond what was needed.
normal.cn: surplus 是表示「超过」的 sur- 加上同一词干，指超出所需的那部分。

normal.en: Plural comes from plures, more than one, which is the same comparative family as plus.
normal.cn: plural 来自 plures（多于一个），与 plus 属于同一个比较级词族。

normal.en: On the plus side is arithmetic turned into judgement: the entries that count in your favour.
normal.cn: on the plus side 是把算术变成判断：那些算在你名下的有利条目。

normal.en: Plus never changes shape: no plural pluses in the arithmetic sense, no past tense, no comparative.
normal.cn: plus 从不改变形态：算术义没有复数，没有过去式，也没有比较级。

abstract.en: A plus is a small hook that pulls the next thing in, which is why it can join numbers and facts alike.
abstract.cn: 加号像一个小钩子，把下一件东西拉进来，所以它能连接数字，也能连接事实。

abstract.en: An advantage is arithmetic done on a life: what is added to your side of the ledger.
abstract.cn: 优势是对人生做的一次算术：添到你这一栏里的东西。

abstract.en: Zero is only a line, and everything on one side of it wears the same mark.
abstract.cn: 零只是一条线，落在它同一侧的东西都带着同一个记号。

examples.en: Two plus three makes five.
examples.cn: 二加三等于五。

examples.en: The rent is three hundred a month, plus electricity.
examples.cn: 房租每月三百，外加电费。

examples.en: A real plus of the flat is the morning light.
examples.cn: 这套房子真正的优点是有早晨的阳光。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普拉丝」——把一根丝线普普通通地拉过来接上，就多出一段；记住 plus 是加。

root: 拉丁语 plus（更多）为比较级形式，词干 plures 意为更多、数个，同族有 surplus（超过之后的剩余）、plural（复数）。英语于十六七世纪借入 plus 用于算术，后引申为正值、额外项目与优势。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one quantity taking in another and becoming more; the senses run from arithmetic addition, to an extra item in a statement, to the positive side of a scale, and finally to a personal advantage.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个数量并入另一个而变多；义项从算术上的相加，走到陈述里追加的一项，再到刻度上为正的一侧，最后落到个人的优势。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pebble on a counting board pushed against another so the two piles become one larger pile.
core.cn: 核心意象：算板上一颗石子被推向另一颗，两堆并成一堆更大的。

branches.en: two pebbles pushed together on a counting board
branches.cn: 算板上并到一起的两颗石子

branches.en: one more name written at the end of a list
branches.cn: 名单末尾又添上的一个名字

branches.en: a thermometer standing above the zero mark
branches.cn: 温度计停在零度线以上

branches.en: a favourable entry in the account book
branches.cn: 账本上一笔有利的记录

branches.en: a second language counted as a strength
branches.cn: 被算作长处的一门第二语言

intro.en: The word is a Latin comparative of quantity, and the family grows by putting prefixes and suffixes around that one stem for more.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示数量的比较级，整族词都是在那一个表示「更多」的词干前后加前缀后缀长出来的。

latinIntro.en: Latin forms are recorded for this word: the comparative plus, more, and its stem plures, more or several.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词有可考的拉丁形式：比较级 plus（更多）及其词干 plures（更多、数个）。

items.meaning: the state of being many, or a majority

definition_zh: 口袋；衣袋；一小块地区；袖珍的；把…据为己有
definition_en: a small bag sewn into clothing for carrying things; a small area or group separated from its surroundings; a smaller than usual version of something; and to take money for oneself, often dishonestly
core_image: 外套内侧缝着一只小布袋，手一探就摸到几枚硬币
scene: 外套挂在门后，手伸进内侧的布兜，摸到几枚温热的硬币。He slid the coins back into his coat pocket and shut the door.
sceneCN: 这里 pocket 是「口袋、衣袋」（第 1 个义项：缝在衣服上、开口朝上的小布袋）；句意为他把硬币塞回外套口袋，关上了门。图中可辨识物件：门后的外套、内侧布兜、硬币。

collocations.zh: 在某人的口袋里；受某人控制

derivatives.zh: 由 pocket 加表示「一…之量」的后缀 -ful 构成，义为「一袋之量」
由 pocket 与 book 复合而成，义为「钱包；袖珍手册」
由 pocket 与 knife 复合而成，义为「随身小折刀」

senses.title: A small bag sewn into clothing
senses.definition: a small bag or piece of cloth sewn into clothing, open at the top, used for carrying small objects
senses.definitionCN: 缝在衣服上、上端开口、用来装小物件的小布袋或布片
senses.example: He kept the key in his trouser pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 他把钥匙放在裤子口袋里。
senses.why: The word began as a name for any small bag, and when such a bag was stitched inside a garment it stopped being carried and became part of what you wear.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初泛指小袋子；当这种小袋子被缝进衣服里面，它就不再被提在手上，而成了穿着之物的一部分。

senses.title: A small area or group set apart
senses.definition: a small area that differs from what surrounds it, or a small separate group of people or things
senses.definitionCN: 与周围环境不同的一小块地方，或与外界分开的一小群人、一小批事物
senses.example: A pocket of resistance held out in the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 山间还有一小股抵抗力量在坚持。
senses.why: A pocket holds things apart from the open space around them, and the same containment is pictured on a map: a small patch or group enclosed by something larger.
senses.whyCN: 口袋把东西与周围的空间隔开，同样的「围住」被搬到了地图上：被更大范围包住的一小块地方或一小群人。

senses.title: Small enough to carry in a pocket
senses.definition: small enough to be carried in a pocket, or made in a smaller size than the usual one
senses.definitionCN: 小得可以装进口袋，或做得比通常尺寸更小的
senses.example: She carried a pocket dictionary to class.
senses.exampleCN: 她带着一本袖珍词典去上课。
senses.why: Once a pocket sets the measure of what can be carried on the body, anything built to that measure earns the word as an adjective: a pocket edition fits where a full one cannot.
senses.whyCN: 口袋一旦成为「能随身带走」的尺度，任何按这个尺度做出来的东西就获得了这个形容词：袖珍版放得进大版本放不进的地方。

senses.title: To take money for oneself
senses.definition: to take or keep money that belongs to another person, especially in a quiet or dishonest way
senses.definitionCN: 把属于别人的钱拿走或留下，尤指悄悄地、不诚实地做
senses.example: The clerk pocketed part of the takings.
senses.exampleCN: 那名职员把一部分营业收入装进了自己腰包。
senses.why: To put something in your pocket is to make it disappear from view and keep it, so the physical act becomes a metaphor for quietly keeping money that was never yours.
senses.whyCN: 把东西放进自己口袋，就是让它从眼前消失并留下，于是这个身体动作变成了暗地里留下不属于自己的钱的比喻。

intro.en: Pocket came into English from Anglo-Norman French for a small bag; the older source of that bag word is usually traced to Germanic, though the exact form is uncertain.
intro.cn: pocket 从盎格鲁-诺曼法语中表示小袋的词进入英语；这个小袋词更早的来源一般认为属日耳曼语族，但确切形式不确定。

items.en: A Germanic word for a bag or pouch is usually thought to lie behind the French forms, but no single source form can be reconstructed with confidence.
items.cn: 一般认为法语中的这些形式背后有一个日耳曼语表示袋子、荷包的词，但无法有把握地重构出唯一源头形式，来源不确定。

items.en: Old French poche named a bag or pouch, a soft container gathered at the top rather than a stiff box.
items.cn: 古法语 poche 指袋子、荷包，是一种上端收拢的软容器，而不是硬邦邦的盒子。

items.en: Anglo-Norman added the diminutive ending -et, so poket named a little bag, the size of a handful.
items.cn: 盎格鲁-诺曼语加上指小词尾 -et，于是 poket 指一只小袋子，大小不过一把。

items.en: Middle English pocket first meant a small pouch and then the pouch sewn into a garment, which is the sense that fixed the word in everyday use.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pocket 先指小袋，后指缝在衣服上的那只袋子，正是这个义项把词固定在了日常用语里。

items.en: Modern English extends the enclosed space to pockets of resistance and pockets of woodland, uses pocket as an adjective for small sizes, and as a verb for quietly keeping money.
items.cn: 现代英语把这种围起来的小空间扩展到一小股抵抗力量、一小片林地，并用 pocket 作形容词表示小尺寸，作动词表示悄悄把钱留下。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same bag stem and two that only echo its shape; the near-meaning group gathers containers and small enclosures.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一个「袋子」词干上的词，另收两个只是形似音近的词；近义组收各类容器与小的封闭空间。

entries.definition: As much as a pocket can hold, formed with the suffix -ful.
entries.definitionCN: 一袋之量；由 pocket 加后缀 -ful 构成。

entries.definition: A wallet or a small notebook, a compound whose first element is pocket.
entries.definitionCN: 钱包或袖珍笔记本；由 pocket 与 book 复合而成。

entries.definition: A small parcel or container; it shares the diminutive ending -et but is built on pack, so the two are close in form only.
entries.definitionCN: 小包、小盒；共享指小词尾 -et，却建立在 pack 之上，只是形式相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A figure moved by strings or by a hand; the similarity is in sound and spelling, and the origin is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 用线或手操纵的人偶；只是读音与拼写相近，来源无关。

entries.definition: A small soft bag, often worn at the waist or forming part of an animal's body.
entries.definitionCN: 柔软的小袋子，常系在腰间，或为动物身体的一部分。

entries.definition: A container of soft material with an opening at the top, used for carrying things.
entries.definitionCN: 用软材料制成、上端开口、用来装东西的容器。

entries.definition: A small flat case for carrying money, cards and papers.
entries.definitionCN: 装钱、卡片与票据的小扁盒。

entries.definition: One of the separate sections into which a space is divided.
entries.definitionCN: 把一处空间分隔开来的其中一格。

normalIntro.en: A French word for a small bag sits at the centre, and the family keeps the picture of something enclosed, held close, and kept out of sight.
normalIntro.cn: 核心是一个法语中表示小袋的词，整族词都保留着「被围住、贴身收着、不让人看见」的画面。

normal.en: Old French poche was a bag, and the ending -et made it a little bag, which is exactly what a pocket is.
normal.cn: 古法语 poche 是袋子，词尾 -et 把它变成小袋子，而口袋正是一只小袋子。

normal.en: The oldest English sense is a pouch carried in the hand; only later was it sewn into clothing and worn.
normal.cn: 英语里最古老的义项是提在手上的小袋，后来它才被缝进衣服穿在身上。

normal.en: Pocket money and pocket-sized both use the same measure: what fits in a pocket, or what is small enough to be spent from one.
normal.cn: pocket money 与 pocket-sized 用的是同一个尺度：装得进口袋，或小得能从口袋里掏出来。

normal.en: Pickpocket names the person and the act together, because the thief reaches for the pocket rather than the bag.
normal.cn: pickpocket 把人跟动作合在一起，因为下手的地方是口袋，不是提包。

normal.en: The verb is regular, and to pocket money is simply to make it vanish into that enclosed space.
normal.cn: 动词变化规则；to pocket money 就是让钱消失进那个围起来的地方。

abstract.en: A pocket is a room in a garment: small, private, and closed to everyone else.
abstract.cn: 口袋是衣服里的一间小屋：狭小、私密，对旁人关着门。

abstract.en: A pocket of resistance is the same shape drawn on a map, a small space held inside a larger one.
abstract.cn: 一小股抵抗力量就是把这个形状画在地图上：被更大范围围住的一小块空间。

abstract.en: To pocket what is not yours is to shrink the world until only your own hand remains in it.
abstract.cn: 把不属于自己的东西据为己有，就是把世界缩小到只剩自己的一只手。

examples.en: He kept the key in his trouser pocket.
examples.cn: 他把钥匙放在裤子口袋里。

examples.en: She carried a pocket dictionary to class.
examples.cn: 她带着一本袖珍词典去上课。

examples.en: The clerk pocketed part of the takings.
examples.cn: 那名职员把一部分营业收入装进了自己腰包。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕磕它」——口袋里装的都是怕磕碰的小东西，手总护着；记住 pocket 是口袋。

root: pocket 来自盎格鲁-诺曼法语 poket，是古法语 poche（袋子）加指小词尾 -et 而成的小袋；poche 更早的来源一般认为属日耳曼语族，但确切形式不确定，也没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a small bag held close to the body; the senses run from the sewn-in pocket, to an enclosed patch on a map, to the size that fits inside one, and finally to the act of quietly keeping what goes in.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一只贴身的小袋子；义项从缝进衣服的口袋，走到地图上被围住的一小块，再到装得进去的尺寸，最后落到悄悄留下放进来的东西这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small cloth bag stitched inside a coat, a hand closing around warm coins.
core.cn: 核心意象：外套内侧缝着的小布袋，手合拢握住几枚温热的硬币。

branches.en: a hand slipping into a coat pocket
branches.cn: 手伸进外套口袋

branches.en: a coin moving from the till into a sleeve
branches.cn: 硬币从钱箱进了袖子

branches.en: a small stand of trees on a bare hill
branches.cn: 光秃山坡上一小片树林

branches.en: a small band holding out in the hills
branches.cn: 山间坚持的一小股人马

branches.en: a dictionary small enough to fit a coat
branches.cn: 小得能塞进外套的词典

intro.en: The word is a French diminutive of a bag noun, and English builds its compounds and its verb from that same enclosed-space picture.
intro.cn: 这个词是法语中「袋子」一词的指小形式，英语又从这个「围起来的小空间」画面造出复合词与动词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; it reached English through French from a bag word usually traced to Germanic, so no Latin entry is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它经法语进入英语，源头一般认为属于日耳曼语族中表示袋子的词，因此不列拉丁条目。

items.meaning: as much as a pocket holds

definition_zh: 诗；诗歌；诗一般的事物
definition_en: a piece of writing arranged in lines, usually with rhythm and often with rhyme, that expresses feeling or thought; the form such works belong to; and something so beautiful or moving that it seems like one
core_image: 一页纸上短行错落，行末的字轻轻碰到一起
scene: 夜里灯下摊着一本薄薄的诗集，行与行之间留出大片空白。She read the poem twice before she understood why it ended with a question.
sceneCN: 这里 poem 是「诗、诗歌」（第 1 个义项：分行排列、讲究节奏的单篇作品）；句意为她读了两遍，才明白这首诗为什么以一个问句收尾。图中可辨识物件：诗集、台灯、行间的大片留白。

derivatives.zh: 与 poem 同出希腊语 poiein（制作），经拉丁语 poeta 进入英语，义为「诗人」
由 poet 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，义为「诗的；富有诗意的」
与 poem 同源，经古法语 poeterie 进入英语，义为「诗歌（总称）；诗艺」

senses.title: A piece of writing in lines
senses.definition: a piece of writing arranged in short lines, usually with rhythm and often with rhyme, that expresses feeling or thought
senses.definitionCN: 分行排列、通常讲究节奏并常有押韵、用来表达情感或想法的作品
senses.example: He copied the poem into the back of his notebook.
senses.exampleCN: 他把那首诗抄在笔记本的末页。
senses.why: Greek poiein meant to make, and a poem was first simply a thing made; what made it special was the shaping of words into measured lines rather than any subject matter.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 poiein 意为制作，诗最初只是「做出来的东西」；使它特别的不是题材，而是把词语排成有节度的行。

senses.title: Verse writing as a form
senses.definition: the form of writing that such works belong to, considered as a genre beside prose and drama
senses.definitionCN: 这类作品所属的写作形式，与散文、戏剧并列的一种文体
senses.example: The poem as a form survived the rise of the novel.
senses.exampleCN: 诗歌作为一种文体，在小说兴起之后依然存续。
senses.why: Once a single made thing is recognised, the whole kind it belongs to can be named by the same word, so poem can stand for the form itself, not just one copy of it.
senses.whyCN: 单件「做出来的东西」一旦被认出来，它所属的整类也能用同一个词来指，于是 poem 能指这种文体本身，而不只是其中一件。

senses.title: Something as beautiful as a poem
senses.titleCN: 诗一般的事物；极美之物
senses.definition: something so beautiful, moving or finely made that it seems like a poem
senses.definitionCN: 美、动人或者做得精巧到像诗一样的事物
senses.example: The garden after rain was a poem in green and silver.
senses.exampleCN: 雨后的园子是一首由绿与银写成的诗。
senses.why: Because a poem is the most compressed and ordered use of language, any scene with the same order and economy can be praised by calling it a poem.
senses.whyCN: 诗是语言最凝练、最有秩序的一种用法，因此任何具备同样秩序与节制的景象，都可以被称作一首诗来称赞。

intro.en: Poem goes back to a Greek verb meaning to make; the thing made became a work in verse, and the word travelled through Latin and French into English.
intro.cn: poem 上溯到一个意为「制作」的希腊语动词；被做出来的东西后来指韵文作品，这个词再经拉丁语与法语进入英语。

items.en: Greek poiein meant to make, to produce or to compose, and it could be used of any craft, not only of writing.
items.cn: 希腊语 poiein 意为制作、产出、创作，可用于任何手艺，并不限于写作。

items.en: The noun poiema named a thing made, a piece of work, and in time it narrowed to a work composed in verse.
items.cn: 名词 poiema 指做出来的东西、一件作品，后来收窄为用韵文写成的作品。

items.en: Latin borrowed poiema as poema, keeping the sense of a poem or a piece of verse, and passed it to the learned writers of Europe.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 poiema 借作 poema，保留了诗、韵文作品的意思，并把它传给欧洲的文人。

items.en: Old French poeme carried the word into ordinary literary use, and English took it over in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 poeme 把这个词带入普通的文学用语，英语在十六世纪把它借了过来。

items.en: Modern English keeps poem for a single work, poetry for the art as a whole, and poet for the maker, all from the same Greek verb.
items.cn: 现代英语用 poem 指单篇作品，用 poetry 指这门艺术整体，用 poet 指创作者，三者同出一个希腊语动词。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Greek verb for making and the family it produced; the near-meaning group gathers kinds of verse and the parts of verse craft.
note.cn: 形近组沿希腊语表示「制作」的动词及其词族展开；近义组收各种诗体与作诗手法。

entries.definition: A person who writes poems; the Greek maker became the maker of verse.
entries.definitionCN: 写诗的人；希腊语里「制作的人」成了作诗的人。

entries.definition: Poems considered as a whole, or the art of writing them.
entries.definitionCN: 作为整体的诗歌，或写诗这门艺术。

entries.definition: Relating to poems, or having the beauty and compression of verse.
entries.definitionCN: 与诗有关的，或具有诗的美的凝练。

entries.definition: The study or theory of poetry as a craft.
entries.definitionCN: 把诗当作一门手艺来研究的学问或理论。

entries.definition: Writing arranged in lines with rhythm, or one line of such writing.
entries.definitionCN: 按节奏分行排列的文字，或其中的一行。

entries.definition: A short poem expressing personal feeling, or the words of a song.
entries.definitionCN: 表达个人情感的短诗，或歌词。

entries.definition: A poem of fourteen lines with a fixed pattern of rhyme.
entries.definitionCN: 十四行、押韵格式固定的诗。

entries.definition: A matching of word endings in sound, or a short poem that uses it.
entries.definitionCN: 词尾读音相合，或使用这种相合的小诗。

normalIntro.en: The whole family grows from one Greek verb for making, so poem, poet and poetry all carry the idea of something crafted rather than merely spoken.
normalIntro.cn: 整族词都从一个希腊语表示「制作」的动词长出来，所以 poem、poet、poetry 都带着「被精心做出来」而不是随口说出的意味。

normal.en: Greek poiein means to make, so a poem is literally something made, like a table or a pot.
normal.cn: 希腊语 poiein 意为制作，所以 poem 字面上就是一件做出来的东西，像桌子或陶罐。

normal.en: Poiema is the thing made, and poema is its Latin form; both point to a finished piece of work rather than to inspiration.
normal.cn: poiema 是做出来的东西，poema 是它的拉丁形式；两者都指向一件完成的作品，而不是灵感。

normal.en: Poet, poem and poetry share the stem: the maker, the single work, and the art as a whole.
normal.cn: poet、poem、poetry 共用一个词干：做的人、单件作品，以及整体的艺术。

normal.en: The difference between poem and poetry is the difference between one chair and carpentry.
normal.cn: poem 与 poetry 的区别，就像一把椅子和木工这门手艺的区别。

normal.en: The word has two syllables, and the second is weak; the plural is simply poems.
normal.cn: 这个词有两个音节，第二个音节很轻；复数直接加 s 变成 poems。

abstract.en: A poem is speech that has been made to slow down, so each word can be looked at.
abstract.cn: 诗是被放慢的说话，好让每个词都值得看一眼。

abstract.en: Line breaks are breaths written down, which is why a poem looks different before it is read aloud.
abstract.cn: 分行是写下来的呼吸，所以一首诗在朗读之前，看上去就不一样。

abstract.en: Calling a garden a poem is a way of saying that order and feeling arrived at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 把园子叫作诗，是在说秩序与情感在同一刻到齐了。

examples.en: He copied the poem into the back of his notebook.
examples.cn: 他把那首诗抄在笔记本的末页。

examples.en: The poem as a form survived the rise of the novel.
examples.cn: 诗歌作为一种文体，在小说兴起之后依然存续。

examples.en: The garden after rain was a poem in green and silver.
examples.cn: 雨后的园子是一首由绿与银写成的诗。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剖木」——把一块木头剖开，削成一行行短句；记住 poem 是诗。

root: 希腊语 poiein（制作）造出 poiema（做出来的东西），拉丁语借作 poema（诗），经古法语 poeme 进入英语；同族有 poet（诗人）、poetry（诗歌总称）、poetic（诗的）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something deliberately made; the senses run from one crafted work in lines, to the whole form of verse writing, and then outward to anything ordered and moving enough to be called a poem.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被有意做出来的东西；义项从一件分行写成的作品，走到韵文写作这种文体，再向外扩展到任何具备同样秩序与动人力量、足以被称作诗的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: short lines stopping well before the margin, with wide white space between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：短行在页边之前就停住，行与行之间留着大片空白。

branches.en: a line ending short of the margin
branches.cn: 行末停在页边之前

branches.en: a page with wide white gaps between the lines
branches.cn: 行间留着大片空白的书页

branches.en: slim volumes of one genre on a shelf
branches.cn: 书架上同一体裁的薄册

branches.en: a critic setting verse beside prose
branches.cn: 评论者把韵文与散文并置

branches.en: a garden shining green after rain
branches.cn: 雨后泛着绿光的花园

intro.en: The word is built on a Greek verb of making and the noun for the thing made, and the same stem gives English the maker, the art and the adjective.
intro.cn: 这个词建立在希腊语表示「制作」的动词与表示「做成之物」的名词上，同一词干又给出英语里的创作者、这门艺术与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin forms are recorded for this word: the borrowed noun poema, a poem, and poeta, the maker of one.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词有可考的拉丁形式：借入的名词 poema（诗）与 poeta（作诗的人）。

definition_zh: 诗人；写诗的人；有诗心的人
definition_en: a person who writes poems, especially one who treats verse as a craft or a calling; also anyone who sees ordinary life with a poet's imagination
core_image: 一个人伏在桌前，把心里翻涌的东西一行行改成有节奏的句子，废纸团堆在脚边
scene: 深夜的屋子里只亮着一盏台灯，纸页被反复涂改，桌边的茶早已凉透。The old poet kept rewriting the last line until dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 poet 是「诗人」（第 1 个义项：以写诗为手艺或志业的人）；句意为这位老诗人反复改写最后一行，一直改到天亮。图中可辨识物件：台灯、涂改过的纸页、凉透的茶杯。

pos.zh: 诗人；写诗的人；有诗心的人

derivatives.zh: 由 poet 换接集合名词后缀 -ry 构成，指诗歌这一体裁的整体
由希腊词干 poie- 加形容词后缀 -tic 构成，义为「诗的；富有诗意的」
由 poetic 加 -s 构成，义为「诗学；诗歌理论」
由 poet 加阴性后缀 -ess 构成，旧指「女诗人」，今已少用

senses.title: A person who writes poems
senses.definition: a person who writes poems, especially one who treats verse as a craft or a calling
senses.definitionCN: 写诗的人，尤指把写诗当作一门手艺或志业的人
senses.example: The poet read three new poems at the small bookshop.
senses.exampleCN: 这位诗人在那家小书店里朗诵了三首新作。
senses.why: Greek poietes began as a word for any maker, and only the habit of calling the verse-maker a maker narrowed it to the writer of poems.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 poietes 原本泛指「制作者」，只是人们习惯把制作诗句的人叫作制作者，词义才收窄为写诗的人。

senses.title: An officially appointed verse writer
senses.definition: a poet formally chosen to write verse for a state, a city or an institution on special occasions
senses.definitionCN: 受国家、城市或机构正式委任，在特定场合献诗的人
senses.example: The poet laureate composed a piece for the coronation.
senses.exampleCN: 桂冠诗人为加冕典礼写了一首诗。
senses.why: When a court or a state wanted verse for its ceremonies, it kept a poet on hand, and that appointment turned the general word into an official title.
senses.whyCN: 当宫廷或国家需要为典礼准备诗句时，会长期供养一位诗人，这个任命就把普通名词变成了官方头衔。

senses.title: A person with a poet's sensibility
senses.titleCN: 有诗心的人；富于想象的人
senses.definition: someone who sees and describes ordinary things with unusual feeling or imagination
senses.definitionCN: 以不寻常的感受力或想象力观察、描述寻常事物的人
senses.example: He is a poet of the kitchen, turning cheap vegetables into something memorable.
senses.exampleCN: 他是厨房里的诗人，能把便宜蔬菜做成令人难忘的东西。
senses.why: If a poet is someone who makes ordinary language carry feeling, then anyone who does that in another craft can borrow the name.
senses.whyCN: 如果诗人就是让寻常语言承载情感的人，那么在任何别的行当里做到这一点的人，都可以借用这个称呼。

senses.title: A representative voice of a tradition
senses.titleCN: 某一诗歌传统的代表作者
senses.definition: a writer whose verse gives a language, an age or a movement its characteristic voice
senses.definitionCN: 其诗作赋予某个语言、时代或流派以鲜明声音的作者
senses.example: The poets of the Harlem Renaissance changed American literature.
senses.exampleCN: 哈莱姆文艺复兴的诗人们改变了美国文学。
senses.why: Because poems are made inside a shared language and a shared moment, the plural poets often names the group that gave a period its sound.
senses.whyCN: 因为诗总是在共同的语言与时代里写成，复数形式 poets 常用来指为一个时期定下声调的那一群人。

intro.en: Poet reaches English through Latin and French from a Greek word that first meant simply a maker, which is still the clearest clue to how the word thinks.
intro.cn: poet 经拉丁语、法语上溯到一个希腊词，那个词最初只表示「制作者」，这仍是理解这个词最清楚的线索。

items.en: The verb poiein meant to make or produce, and it was used of anything brought into being, not only verse.
items.cn: 动词 poiein 意为制作、产出，凡被做出来的东西都可以用它，并不专指诗句。

items.en: A poietes was a maker; calling the writer of verse the maker gradually made the noun mean poet.
items.cn: poietes 是「制作者」；把写诗的人称作制作者，这个名词就渐渐专指诗人。

items.en: Latin took poeta from Greek as a loan; the form is borrowed rather than native, so it does not follow ordinary Latin noun patterns.
items.cn: 拉丁语 poeta 借自希腊语，是外来借词而非本土词，所以词形不遵循一般拉丁名词的规律。

items.en: Old French poete carried the word into medieval literary life and passed it to English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 poete 把这个词带入中世纪的文学生活，并在诺曼时期之后传给英语。

items.en: English poet keeps the old idea that a poem is something made, while poet laureate adds an official, salaried role.
items.cn: 英语 poet 保留了「诗是被制作出来的东西」这一古老观念，而 poet laureate 又添上了带薪的官方身份。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same Greek making stem; the near-meaning group collects other names for people who write or recite.
note.cn: 形近组收同一希腊「制作」词干上的词；近义组收写诗、吟诵者的其他称呼。

entries.definition: Verse as a whole, the art this person practises.
entries.definitionCN: 诗歌总称；这个人所从事的这门艺术。

entries.definition: Written in verse, or full of the beauty associated with it.
entries.definitionCN: 以诗体写成的；富有诗意的。

entries.definition: A single piece of verse, countable where the collective noun is not.
entries.definitionCN: 单篇诗作，可数，与不可数的集合名词相对。

entries.definition: An old word for a woman who writes verse, now rarely used.
entries.definitionCN: 旧时指女诗人的词，今已少用。

entries.definition: An old word for a poet, especially a national or wandering one.
entries.definitionCN: 旧时指诗人，尤指民族诗人或行吟诗人。

entries.definition: A person who writes the words of songs.
entries.definitionCN: 为歌曲写词的人。

entries.definition: A person who produces books, stories or articles of any kind.
entries.definitionCN: 写书、写故事或写各类文章的人。

entries.definition: The person who originates a written work.
entries.definitionCN: 一部文字作品的创作者。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Greek making verb turned into a person, and the family around it keeps that same workshop image.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是把希腊语的「制作」动词变成一个人，围绕它的整族词都保留着同一幅作坊画面。

normal.en: Poet goes back to Greek poiein, to make, so the word calls a poem a thing made rather than a thing merely felt.
normal.cn: poet 上溯到希腊语 poiein（制作），所以这个词把诗看成做出来的东西，而不只是感受到的东西。

normal.en: The Greek agent ending -tes marks the doer, much as -er does in maker, so poietes is literally a maker.
normal.cn: 希腊语施事后缀 -tes 标示动作的执行者，作用近似 maker 里的 -er，所以 poietes 字面就是「制作者」。

normal.en: Poetry keeps the same stem but takes a collective ending: the art and its whole body of works, not one person.
normal.cn: poetry 保留同一词干却接了集合词尾：指这门艺术与全部作品，而不是一个人。

normal.en: Poetic adds the adjective ending -ic and describes the quality, which is why a sunset can be poetic with no verse in sight.
normal.cn: poetic 加形容词词尾 -ic，描述的是性质，所以一场日落即使没有半句诗也可以是诗意的。

normal.en: Latin poeta is a Greek loan, so no native Latin root should be invented to explain the shape.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 poeta 是希腊借词，不该为解释这个词形去编造拉丁本土词根。

abstract.en: A culture that names its poets makers is saying that language is material to be worked, not just air to be breathed.
abstract.cn: 一个把诗人称作「制作者」的文化是在说：语言是可以加工的材料，而不只是呼吸间的空气。

abstract.en: The same noun stretches from a person at a desk to a cook at a stove, because the act being named is shaping, not writing.
abstract.cn: 同一个名词从书桌前的人延伸到灶台前的厨师，因为被命名的是「塑形」这个动作，而不是写字。

abstract.en: Call someone a poet of a place and you grant that place a voice it did not have before.
abstract.cn: 把某人称作某地的诗人，等于承认那个地方从此有了过去没有的声音。

examples.en: The poet spent the morning revising a single stanza.
examples.cn: 这位诗人花了一上午修改一节诗。

examples.en: She is a poet of small-town life rather than of grand events.
examples.cn: 她是小镇生活的诗人，而不是写宏大事件的诗人。

examples.en: The poem was published without the poet's name.
examples.cn: 这首诗发表时没有署诗人的名字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼伊特」——诗人把心里的东西一股脑泼在纸上，再一个字一个字拾起来排好。

root: 希腊语 poiein（制作）→ poietes（制作者、诗人）→ 拉丁语 poeta（借自希腊语）→ 古法语 poete → 英语 poet。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the maker of verse; from it come the appointed ceremonial voice, the borrowed praise for any imaginative worker, and the collective name for a school.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「诗句的制作者」；由此分出受任的典礼声音、借来形容任何富有想象力的行当的称呼，以及指一个流派的集合用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone bent over a desk at night, turning a surge of feeling into lines with a rhythm, crumpled paper at their feet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人夜里伏在桌前，把翻涌的情绪改写成有节奏的句子，脚边堆着揉皱的纸。

branches.en: a writer at a desk and a writer on a ceremonial stage
branches.cn: 书桌前写作的人与典礼台上献诗的人

branches.en: a cook describing a bowl of soup as if it were a sonnet
branches.cn: 厨师把一碗汤说得像一首十四行诗

branches.en: a generation of writers giving an age its sound
branches.cn: 一代作家为一个时代定下声调

branches.en: one stanza revised until it finally stands
branches.cn: 一节诗被改到终于立住

branches.en: one name for an appointed role and for a shared tradition
branches.cn: 同一个称呼既指受任的角色，也指共享的传统

intro.en: A Greek verb of making supplies the root, a Greek agent ending makes it a person, and Latin and French pass the shape to English.
intro.cn: 一个表示制作的希腊动词提供词根，一个希腊施事后缀把它变成人，再经拉丁语与法语把词形传给英语。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaningCN: 希腊语施事后缀：做……的人

definition_zh: 诗歌（总称）；诗艺；诗意；韵文
definition_en: poems considered as a whole, as a form of literature; also the art of writing them, the quality of beauty they carry, and verse as a medium opposed to prose
core_image: 书架上并排立着许多薄薄的诗集，翻开的一页字句稀疏，空白比墨迹更多
scene: 雨夜的图书馆里只剩翻页的轻响，靠窗的桌上摊着一本薄薄的诗集。She read poetry aloud to the empty room, pausing after every line.
sceneCN: 这里 poetry 指「诗歌」这个整体（第 1 个义项：作为文学体裁的诗歌总称，不可数，与可数的 poem 相对）；句意为她对着空房间朗读诗歌，每读完一行就停一停。图中可辨识物件：翻开的诗集、窗上的雨痕、台灯。

pos.zh: 诗歌（总称）；诗艺；诗意；韵文

forms.label: 不可数名词，通常无复数

derivatives.zh: 同源词，去掉集合词尾 -ry 后指写诗的人
同源词，指一首具体的诗，可数，与不可数的 poetry 分工不同
由希腊词干 poie- 加 -tic 构成，义为「诗的；富有诗意的」
由 poetic 加 -s 构成，义为「诗学」

senses.title: Poems considered as a whole
senses.definition: poems taken together as a body of writing and as a form of literature, used as an uncountable noun
senses.definitionCN: 把诗作作为一个整体来看的文学体裁，作不可数名词使用
senses.example: Her shelf holds more poetry than fiction.
senses.exampleCN: 她书架上的诗集比小说还多。
senses.why: The -ry ending that English took from French marks a collectivity, so poetry gathers many separate poems into one mass and therefore takes no plural.
senses.whyCN: 英语从法语借来的 -ry 词尾表示集合，于是 poetry 把许多首独立的诗收成一个整体，因此没有复数形式。

senses.title: The art of writing poems
senses.definition: the craft of composing verse, including rhythm, line breaks and image
senses.definitionCN: 写作诗句的手艺，包括节奏、分行与意象
senses.example: He studied the poetry of the eighteenth century as a craft rather than a mood.
senses.exampleCN: 他把十八世纪的诗当作一门手艺来研究，而不是当作一种情绪。
senses.why: Latin poesis named the making before it named the made thing, so the craft sense is the older one rather than a later metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 poesis 先指「制作」这个动作，再指做成的东西，所以「诗艺」义其实更早，并不是后来的比喻。

senses.title: A quality of beauty or feeling
senses.definition: a quality in a place, an action or an object that stirs feeling the way a poem does
senses.definitionCN: 某个地方、动作或物件身上那种像诗一样打动人的品质
senses.example: There is poetry in the way a fishing boat turns back at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 渔船在黄昏掉头回港的样子，自有一种诗意。
senses.why: Once the word meant the crafted arrangement of words, it could be lent to any arrangement of things that moves a person in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词曾指对词语的精心安排，它就可以被借去形容任何能同样打动人的事物安排。

senses.title: Verse as a medium, opposed to prose
senses.definition: language shaped by rhythm and line rather than by the ordinary order of sentences
senses.definitionCN: 由节奏与分行塑形、而非依照普通句子顺序排列的语言
senses.example: The story shifts from prose into poetry in its final pages.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事在最后几页从散文转成了诗体。
senses.why: A poem is recognised first by its shape on the page and in the ear, so poetry also names the medium itself, set against prose.
senses.whyCN: 诗最先被人认出的是它在纸面上和耳朵里的形态，所以 poetry 也指这种媒介本身，与散文相对。

intro.en: Poetry and poet share one Greek stem, but poetry took a collective ending and settled as the uncountable name of the whole art.
intro.cn: poetry 与 poet 共用一个希腊词干，但 poetry 接了集合词尾，固定为指整门艺术而不可数的名称。

items.en: The verb poiein meant to make or compose, the ordinary word for producing anything.
items.cn: 动词 poiein 意为制作、编写，是制作任何东西时最普通的说法。

items.en: The noun poiēsis named a making or a composition, and could be used of the making of a poem.
items.cn: 名词 poiēsis 指制作或作品，也可以用来指一首诗的作成。

items.en: Latin used poesis for verse and poeta for the writer; both were learned borrowings from Greek.
items.cn: 拉丁语用 poesis 指诗，用 poeta 指写诗的人，两者都是从希腊语借来的学术词。

items.en: Old French poetrie, also written poeterie, named both the art and the collected verse, with a suffix that marks a body of things.
items.cn: 古法语 poetrie（也写作 poeterie）既指这门艺术，也指收集起来的诗作，词尾本身带有「一批事物」的集合意味。

items.en: English poetry settled as the uncountable term for the whole field, leaving poem as the countable word for one work.
items.cn: 英语 poetry 固定为指整个领域的不可数词，而单篇作品留给可数的 poem。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same making family, where the countable unit and the adjective sit beside the collective noun; the near-meaning group gathers other words of the verse trade.
note.cn: 形近组是同一个「制作」词族，可数单位与形容词都挨着这个集合名词；近义组收诗歌行当里的其他词。

entries.definition: One single piece of verse, countable, the unit that the collective noun gathers.
entries.definitionCN: 单篇诗作，可数，正是集合名词所收的单位。

entries.definition: Of verse, or having the beauty associated with it.
entries.definitionCN: 诗体的；富有诗意的。

entries.definition: The person who makes poems; the collective noun adds its ending to the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 写诗的人；集合名词是在同一词干上加词尾而成。

entries.definition: The theory or systematic study of verse.
entries.definitionCN: 诗学；对诗歌的系统研究。

entries.definition: Writing arranged in lines, usually with rhythm; also a single line.
entries.definitionCN: 分行写成的文字，通常有节奏；也可指一行诗。

entries.definition: Ordinary written language without line breaks, the counterpart of verse.
entries.definitionCN: 不按诗行排列的普通书面语，与韵文相对。

entries.definition: The matching of sounds at the ends of lines.
entries.definitionCN: 诗行末尾音韵相合。

entries.definition: A short poem of personal feeling, often meant to be sung.
entries.definitionCN: 表达个人情感的短诗，常可歌唱。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Greek noun of making with a collective ending, and that ending is the whole difference between one poem and the art itself.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是带集合词尾的希腊「制作」名词，而这个词尾正是一首诗与整门艺术之间的全部差别。

normal.en: Poetry shares its stem with poet, but the -ry ending turns a person into a whole field of work.
normal.cn: poetry 与 poet 共用词干，但 -ry 词尾把一个人变成了一整片工作领域。

normal.en: Poem is the countable unit and poetry is the uncountable mass, so we say a poem but never a poetry.
normal.cn: poem 是可数的单位，poetry 是不可数的整体，所以说 a poem，却不说 a poetry。

normal.en: Greek poiēsis meant a making, which is why poetry can name the craft and not only the finished texts.
normal.cn: 希腊语 poiēsis 意为制作，所以 poetry 既能指手艺，也能指成品。

normal.en: Poetic keeps the adjective ending -ic and describes the quality, while poetry names the thing itself.
normal.cn: poetic 保留形容词词尾 -ic 来描述性质，poetry 则指事物本身。

normal.en: The plural poems is normal for separate works, but poetry stays singular even when it covers centuries.
normal.cn: 分开的作品用复数 poems 很正常，而 poetry 即使涵盖几个世纪也仍是单数。

abstract.en: A language that keeps a separate uncountable word for verse is treating poems as a substance rather than a list.
abstract.cn: 一种语言若为诗保留一个独立的不可数词，就是把诗当成一种物质，而不是一份清单。

abstract.en: The same word covers a craft and a feeling, which suggests that technique and emotion were never meant to be separated here.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指手艺又指感受，这说明在这个领域里技巧与情感从来不该被分开。

abstract.en: Saying there is poetry in a harbour is a quiet claim that the world can be arranged like a line.
abstract.cn: 说一个港湾里有诗意，是在轻声主张：世界也可以像一行诗那样被安排。

examples.en: She writes poetry in the mornings before work.
examples.cn: 她在上班前的早晨写诗。

examples.en: The anthology traces four centuries of Chinese poetry.
examples.cn: 这部选集梳理了中国诗歌四百年的脉络。

examples.en: There was a strange poetry in the empty station at midnight.
examples.cn: 午夜空旷的车站里有一种奇特的诗意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剖厄特里」——把一首诗剖开，里面是一层层的节奏、分行与意象。

root: 希腊语 poiein（制作）→ poiēsis（制作、诗作）→ 拉丁语 poesis（借自希腊语）→ 古法语 poetrie（诗艺、诗作）→ 英语 poetry；词尾 -ry 表集合。

sensesIntro.en: The core is verse taken as a whole; the senses divide into the craft, the feeling it leaves behind, and the medium that stands against prose.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是作为整体的诗；义项分为这门手艺、它留下的感受，以及与散文相对的媒介。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: thin volumes standing side by side on a shelf, an open page with wide margins where the white space speaks as much as the ink.
core.cn: 核心意象：书架上并排立着薄薄的诗集，翻开的一页留白很宽，空白几乎和墨迹一样在说话。

branches.en: a shelf where thin volumes outnumber novels
branches.cn: 书架上薄薄的诗集比小说还多

branches.en: a hand counting beats while shaping a line
branches.cn: 一只手打着拍子把一行字排好

branches.en: a harbour at dusk that feels like a stanza
branches.cn: 黄昏的港湾像一节诗

branches.en: a page breaking from paragraphs into lines
branches.cn: 页面从成段文字断成一行行

branches.en: one word for printed books and for a feeling in the air
branches.cn: 同一个词既指印成的书，也指空气里的感受

intro.en: A Greek verb of making, its noun of process, a Latin loan and a French collective ending all meet in this one word.
intro.cn: 一个表示制作的希腊动词、它的过程名词、一个拉丁借词和一个法语集合词尾，在这一个词里汇合。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: the art and body of verse

items.meaningCN: 集合后缀：一批事物或一门技艺

definition_zh: 要点；得分；地点；小数点；指向
definition_en: the main idea of what someone says; a unit of score; an exact place or moment; the dot in a decimal number; also to aim or show direction
core_image: 一根手指伸出去停在半空，所有人的视线顺着这条线落到墙上同一个位置
scene: 会议室里的讨论拖了很久，白板上写满潦草的字，有人忽然把笔尖按在其中一个词上。She tapped the board and made her point in one short sentence.
sceneCN: 这里 point 指「要点」（第 1 个义项：说话人最想让人记住的那一点）；句意为她敲了敲白板，用一句短话把自己的要点说清楚。图中可辨识物件：写满字的白板、按在词上的笔尖、几张转过来的脸。

derivatives.zh: 由 point 加 -ed 构成，义为「尖的；有针对性的」
由 point 加 -er 构成，义为「指示棒；提示；指针」
由 point 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无意义的；没有尖头的」
与 point 同出拉丁语 punctum，义为「准时的」，原指恰好落在某一刻

senses.title: The main idea in what is said
senses.definition: the central idea that a speaker or writer wants to be understood and remembered
senses.definitionCN: 说话人或作者最想让人理解并记住的那个中心意思
senses.example: Her point was that the plan costs far too much.
senses.exampleCN: 她的要点是这个方案花费太高。
senses.why: Latin punctum named the small mark left by a prick, and a mark is exactly what you put beside the one thing that must not be missed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 punctum 指被刺出的小痕，而人们正是用记号标出那件绝不能漏掉的事。

senses.title: A unit of score in a game or test
senses.definition: one of the units by which a game, a contest or an examination is measured
senses.definitionCN: 衡量一场比赛、一次竞赛或一场考试的计量单位
senses.example: He won the final point with a serve down the line.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一记压边线的发球拿下了最后一分。
senses.why: A score was once kept by making a small mark for each success, so the mark itself became the unit of winning.
senses.whyCN: 过去记分就是每得一分画一个小记号，于是记号本身成了计量的单位。

senses.title: A particular place or moment
senses.definition: an exact spot on a map, a body or a scale, or a particular moment in time
senses.definitionCN: 地图、身体或刻度上确切的一处，或时间上特定的某一刻
senses.example: We met at the point where the two roads meet.
senses.exampleCN: 我们约在两条路交汇的那一点见面。
senses.why: A dot fixes a position and nothing else, which is why the same noun can pin down a place on a map and a moment on a timeline.
senses.whyCN: 一个点只固定位置，别的什么也不带，所以同一个名词既能标定地图上的一处，也能标定时间轴上的一刻。

senses.title: The dot in a decimal number
senses.definition: the mark that separates the whole part of a number from its fraction
senses.definitionCN: 把一个数的整数部分与小数部分分开的记号
senses.example: The reading was three point seven metres.
senses.exampleCN: 读数是三点七米。
senses.why: Because the dot is literally a small prick on the page, the mark that splits a decimal simply inherited the name of the mark itself.
senses.whyCN: 因为那个点字面上就是纸上的一个小刺痕，分开整数与小数的记号便直接继承了「记号」这个名字。

senses.title: To aim or show direction
senses.definition: to turn a finger or an object towards something, or to show what is true or likely
senses.definitionCN: 把手指或物体转向某处，或显示出什么是真的、什么是可能发生的
senses.example: The arrow points north along the coastal path.
senses.exampleCN: 箭头指向沿海小路的北面。
senses.why: A pointed finger and a written dot do the same job, both singling out one thing among many, so the noun turned into a verb of directing attention.
senses.whyCN: 伸出的手指与纸上的点做的是同一件事，都是在众多事物里单单挑出一个，于是名词转成了引导注意的动词。

intro.en: Point comes from a Latin word for a prick and the mark it leaves; the dot is the oldest picture behind the score, the argument and the pointing finger.
intro.cn: point 出自拉丁语中表示「刺」的词以及刺出的痕迹；那个小点，就是得分、论点与指路手指背后最古老的画面。

items.en: The verb pungere meant to prick or pierce, the action of a sharp tip against a surface.
items.cn: 动词 pungere 意为刺、扎，是尖锐之物抵住表面的动作。

items.en: Its neuter past participle punctum named the tiny mark or hole left behind, and so came to mean a dot.
items.cn: 它的中性过去分词 punctum 指留下的细微痕迹或小孔，于是有了「点」的意思。

items.en: Old French point carried the dot, but also a stitch, a moment and a item in an argument.
items.cn: 古法语 point 既保留「点」，也指针脚、某一刻以及论述中的一项。

items.en: English took point first for a dot or a sharp end, then for a mark in a game and the chief item of a speech.
items.cn: 英语先以 point 指点状物或尖端，随后指比赛中的记号与讲话里的主要一项。

items.en: Modern English adds the decimal point, the pointing gesture, point of view, and dozens of fixed phrases.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上小数点、指点的动作、point of view 以及大量固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group stays on the Latin prick and its mark; the near-meaning group gathers the dot, the score, the stage and the act of aiming.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁语「刺」及其痕迹展开；近义组收点、得分、阶段与瞄准这些意思。

entries.definition: Having a sharp end, or clearly aimed at one person.
entries.definitionCN: 有尖端的；明显针对某一个人的。

entries.definition: A stick, cursor or hint that shows where to look.
entries.definitionCN: 指示棒、光标或提示。

entries.definition: Having no purpose or result at all.
entries.definitionCN: 完全没有目的或结果的。

entries.definition: Arriving exactly at the agreed time.
entries.definitionCN: 恰好在约定时刻到达的。

entries.definition: The marks such as commas and full stops used in writing.
entries.definitionCN: 书写中使用的逗号、句号等标记。

entries.definition: A small round mark.
entries.definitionCN: 小而圆的点。

entries.definition: The number of points won in a game.
entries.definitionCN: 比赛中赢得的分数。

entries.definition: A particular point in a process or development.
entries.definitionCN: 过程或发展中的某一阶段。

entries.definition: To point or direct something at a target.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物对准目标。

normalIntro.en: Everything here grows from one tiny mark made by a sharp tip, and that mark still explains the score, the argument and the finger.
normalIntro.cn: 这里的一切都长自尖端留下的一个小记号，而这个记号至今能解释得分、论点与手指。

normal.en: Pungere means to prick, and punctum is the mark a prick leaves, so every sense starts from a tiny mark.
normal.cn: pungere 意为刺，punctum 是刺出的小痕，所以每个义项都从这一个小记号出发。

normal.en: To point at something is to put an invisible dot on it, which is why the noun became a verb.
normal.cn: 指着某物，等于在它上面放一个看不见的点，名词就这样变成了动词。

normal.en: A point in a game was once a tally mark, so the score and the dot are the same mark seen twice.
normal.cn: 比赛中的一分原本就是一个记数记号，所以得分与点其实是同一个记号的两次现身。

normal.en: The decimal point is a real dot on the page, and it is the oldest physical sense surviving almost unchanged.
normal.cn: 小数点是纸上真实的一点，也是几乎原封不动留存下来的最古老的实指义。

normal.en: Pointless adds -less, without a point, and the metaphor is still visible: something with nothing to aim at.
normal.cn: pointless 加 -less，意为「没有点」，比喻仍然看得见：没有可瞄准之处。

abstract.en: The same mark that measures a game also marks the one sentence worth remembering, which says how close play and argument are.
abstract.cn: 衡量比赛的记号也被用来标出那句值得记住的话，可见游戏与论辩有多近。

abstract.en: A point is a decision about where to stop: a dot chooses a place on a map the way a conclusion chooses a place in an argument.
abstract.cn: 一个点就是决定在哪里停下：圆点在地图上选定一处，正如结论在论述中选定一处。

abstract.en: When someone says you have missed the point, the image is still spatial, as if the meaning had a location you walked past.
abstract.cn: 当有人说你错过了要点，这个说法仍是空间性的，仿佛意义有一个你走过了的位置。

examples.en: Let me make one point before we vote.
examples.cn: 在投票之前，请让我说明一点。

examples.en: She has already scored twenty points this season.
examples.cn: 这个赛季她已经得了二十分。

examples.en: From this point the road climbs steeply.
examples.cn: 从这里开始，路陡然向上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剖因特」——手指一剖，直直对着那一个点，不偏不倚。

root: 拉丁语 pungere（刺）→ 过去分词 punctum（刺出的点、记号）→ 古法语 point → 英语 point。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a mark made by a sharp tip; from it come the idea worth marking, the tally of a game, a fixed spot in space or time, the decimal dot and the act of aiming.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是尖端留下的一个记号；由此生出值得标记的意思、比赛的记数、时空中的定点、小数点以及瞄准的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger held out and stopped in mid-air, every eye in the room following the line to one spot on the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指伸出后停在半空，满屋的视线都顺着这条线落在墙上同一处。

branches.en: a sentence that makes a long meeting fall into place
branches.cn: 一句话让冗长的会议落到实处

branches.en: a serve landing just inside the line
branches.cn: 一记刚好落在边线内的发球

branches.en: two roads meeting at one exact spot
branches.cn: 两条路交于确切的一点

branches.en: a dot splitting a number in two
branches.cn: 一个点把数字分成两半

branches.en: a finger and a sentence both singling out one thing
branches.cn: 手指与句子都在挑出同一件事

intro.en: A Latin verb of pricking, its participle turned noun, and a French borrowing together supply the whole family of marks and aims.
intro.cn: 一个表示刺的拉丁动词、由分词转成的名词，加上一次法语借入，共同支撑起这整族关于记号与瞄准的词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 极；极点；杆；磁极；电极；对立的一端
definition_en: either end of an axis, a long slender rod, or one of two opposite extremes
core_image: 地球的自转轴从球心穿出，两端各有一个点；旁边另立一根笔直的长木杆
scene: 河边的船工撑起木筏准备过浅滩。The boatman pushes the raft along the river with a long pole.
sceneCN: 这里 pole 指「一根细长的木杆或金属杆」（第 2 个义项：用于撑船、支撑或探测的长杆）；句意为船工用长杆把木筏撑过河面。图中可辨识物件：木筏、长杆、浅滩、河水；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 极的；极性的
向极地的
北极星；指导原则
旗杆
长柄斧；用斧砍倒
撑杆跳

senses.title: Either end of the earth's axis
senses.titleCN: 地极：地球自转轴的两端
senses.definition: either of the two points where the earth's axis of rotation meets its surface
senses.definitionCN: 地球自转轴与地表相交的两个点之一
senses.example: Expeditions race to reach the South Pole.
senses.exampleCN: 探险队竞相抵达南极点。
senses.why: Greek polos named the pivot of a turning sphere; the two ends of that axis are the poles.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 polos 指旋转球体的枢轴；这条轴的两端就是极。

senses.title: A long slender rod
senses.titleCN: 杆：细长的木杆或金属杆
senses.definition: a long slender piece of wood or metal used for support, pushing or fishing
senses.definitionCN: 用于支撑、撑推或钓鱼的细长木杆或金属杆
senses.example: He planted a pole to mark the boundary.
senses.exampleCN: 他竖了一根杆子来标出边界。
senses.why: This sense has a different origin: Old English pāl 'stake' from Latin palus 'stake', not from Greek polos.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项来源不同：古英语 pāl「桩」来自拉丁 palus「桩」，而非希腊 polos。

senses.title: A magnetic pole
senses.titleCN: 磁极：磁体磁力最强的两端
senses.definition: either of the two ends of a magnet where the magnetic force is concentrated
senses.definitionCN: 磁体两端磁力集中的任一端
senses.example: Like poles repel each other.
senses.exampleCN: 同名的磁极互相排斥。
senses.why: Magnetism was pictured as an axis with two ends, so those ends took the name of the earth's poles.
senses.whyCN: 磁现象被想象成一条有两端的轴，这两端便沿用了地球「极」的名称。

senses.title: An electric terminal
senses.titleCN: 电极：电源或电路的正负端
senses.definition: either of the two terminals of an electric cell or circuit
senses.definitionCN: 电池或电路的两个端子之一
senses.example: Connect the red wire to the positive pole.
senses.exampleCN: 把红线接到正极。
senses.why: Electricity inherited the two-end image from magnetism, so a battery's terminals are also poles.
senses.whyCN: 电学从磁学继承了「两端」的意象，因此电池端子也叫极。

senses.title: One of two opposite extremes
senses.titleCN: 对立的一端：两个极端之一
senses.definition: either of two opposite positions, opinions or tendencies
senses.definitionCN: 两个对立立场、观点或倾向中的任一方
senses.example: The two candidates represent opposite poles of the party.
senses.exampleCN: 两位候选人代表党内对立的两端。
senses.why: Two poles of an axis face opposite directions, which makes them a natural image for extreme opposition.
senses.whyCN: 同一轴的两极朝向相反，因此自然成为极端对立的意象。

senses.title: The pole of a circle or sphere
senses.titleCN: 极点：几何中与给定圆或球对应的点
senses.definition: a point related to a circle or sphere by a fixed geometric construction
senses.definitionCN: 与给定圆或球通过固定几何构造相联系的点
senses.example: The pole of the great circle lies on the perpendicular axis.
senses.exampleCN: 这个大圆的极点位于垂直轴上。
senses.why: Projective geometry keeps the axis-end meaning but defines the point by a relation instead of by the earth.
senses.whyCN: 射影几何保留了「轴端」之义，但用几何关系而非地球来定义这个点。

senses.title: A unit of length
senses.titleCN: 杆：英制长度单位，约五码半
senses.definition: a former unit of length equal to about five and a half yards, used in surveying
senses.definitionCN: 旧时长度单位，约合五码半，用于测量
senses.example: The field measured ten poles across.
senses.exampleCN: 这块地横量有十杆宽。
senses.why: The measuring rod itself became the unit, so a pole could mean both the stick and the length it marked.
senses.whyCN: 测量用的杆本身成了单位，因此 pole 既可指杆，也可指它所标的长度。

senses.title: A pole of a dividing cell
senses.titleCN: 细胞极：有丝分裂纺锤体的两端
senses.definition: either of the two ends of the spindle in a dividing cell, toward which chromosomes move
senses.definitionCN: 分裂细胞纺锤体的两端，染色体分别移向那里
senses.example: The spindle fibres pull chromosomes toward each pole.
senses.exampleCN: 纺锤丝把染色体拉向两极。
senses.why: A dividing cell behaves like a tiny sphere with an axis, so its spindle ends are called poles.
senses.whyCN: 分裂的细胞像带轴的小球，因此纺锤体两端被称为极。

intro.en: Pole has two separate origins that happen to share a spelling: the geographic and magnetic pole from Greek polos 'axis', and the rod from Old English pāl 'stake', from Latin palus. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pole 有两个恰好同形的来源：地理与磁学的「极」来自希腊 polos「轴」，而「杆」来自古英语 pāl「桩」，再上溯拉丁 palus。年代均为约数。

items.en: Polos meant 'pivot, axis, end of an axis'. Its deeper origin is not established, and links to a 'turn' root are hypotheses.
items.cn: polos 意为「枢轴、轴、轴端」。其更深来源未得到证明，与「转动」词根的联系属假说。

items.en: Latin polus 'pole, especially of the heavens' was borrowed from Greek and passed into English as pole.
items.cn: 拉丁 polus「极，尤指天极」借自希腊语，后进入英语作 pole。

items.en: The rod sense comes from Old English pāl 'stake, post', borrowed from Latin palus 'stake'. Palus 'stake' is a different word from palus 'marsh'.
items.cn: 「杆」义来自古英语 pāl「桩、柱」，借自拉丁 palus「桩」。palus「桩」与 palus「沼泽」是两个不同的词。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the ends of a magnet were called poles by analogy with the earth's axis.
items.cn: 16 世纪起，磁体两端因类比地球轴端而被称为极。

items.en: By the seventeenth century 'poles apart' and 'opposite poles' extended the axis image to opinions and positions.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，poles apart 与 opposite poles 把轴端意象扩展到观点与立场。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates only): the exact first English use of the unit of length and of the cell-biology sense is not recorded; the two roots themselves are well documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：长度单位与细胞生物学义在英语中的确切首见年代未见记录；两个词根本身都有充分文献。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound like pole; group two holds rods, ends and extremes.
note.cn: 第一组是外形或读音接近 pole 的词；第二组是关于杆、端点与极端的词。

entries.definition: A survey of opinions or a vote; it sounds identical to pole but has no axis or rod meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 指民意调查或投票；与 pole 同音，但没有轴或杆的意思。

entries.definition: Light in colour, or a boundary stake; the vowel is different from pole.
entries.definitionCN: 颜色浅的，或指界桩；元音与 pole 不同。

entries.definition: A small body of water or a shared fund; the vowel is long and different.
entries.definitionCN: 小水塘或共用资金；元音更长且不同。

entries.definition: A small burrowing animal or a spot on the skin; it shares the ending but not the meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 穴居小动物或皮肤上的痣；词尾相同而意义无关。

entries.definition: A strong upright piece of timber or metal fixed in the ground; a pole may be movable and thinner.
entries.definitionCN: 固定在地上的坚固立木或金属柱；pole 可能更细且可移动。

entries.definition: A slim straight bar of wood or metal; pole is longer and often used for pushing.
entries.definitionCN: 细直的木条或金属条；pole 更长，常用于撑推。

entries.definition: A heavy horizontal timber or metal bar that carries a load; it is structural, unlike a simple pole.
entries.definitionCN: 承重的粗大水平木梁或金属梁；它是结构件，不同于普通杆。

entries.definition: The furthest point or most intense degree; a pole is one of two extremes facing each other.
entries.definitionCN: 最远的点或最强的程度；pole 是彼此相对的两个极端之一。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: two real roots, real magnetism and real surveying, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实词根、真实的磁学与真实的测量，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Geographic pole comes from Greek polos 'axis'; rod pole comes from Latin palus 'stake'. Same spelling, different roots.
normal.cn: 地理的 pole 来自希腊 polos「轴」；杆义的 pole 来自拉丁 palus「桩」。同形不同源。

normal.en: The North Pole and South Pole are the two ends of the earth's rotation axis.
normal.cn: 北极与南极是地球自转轴的两端。

normal.en: Like magnetic poles repel, unlike poles attract.
normal.cn: 同名磁极相斥，异名磁极相吸。

normal.en: A battery has a positive pole and a negative pole.
normal.cn: 电池有正极与负极。

normal.en: Poles apart means as far apart as the two ends of an axis.
normal.cn: poles apart 意为像轴的两端那样相距极远。

abstract.en: Picture two flags planted at the ends of a long straight road.
abstract.cn: 想象一条笔直长路的两端各插一面旗。

abstract.en: Picture a see-saw with one end up and the other down.
abstract.cn: 想象一块跷跷板，一端翘起、一端落下。

abstract.en: Picture a tent held up by one simple straight stick.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶帐篷只靠一根笔直的棍子撑起。

examples.en: The expedition reached the North Pole by dog sled.
examples.cn: 探险队乘狗拉雪橇抵达北极。

examples.en: He vaulted over the fence with a long pole.
examples.cn: 他用一根长杆撑过栅栏。

examples.en: Their political views are poles apart.
examples.cn: 他们的政治观点截然相反。

dict_mnemonic.text: pole 有两个来源：地理「极」来自希腊轴心，长「杆」来自拉丁木桩；同形两义 → 极、杆

root: 地理与磁学的 pole 来自希腊 polos「轴」经拉丁 polus；杆义的 pole 来自古英语 pāl「桩」，再上溯拉丁 palus「桩」。两源同形异义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses divide between an axis and a rod: the earth's two ends, a long stick, magnetic and electric terminals, opposite extremes, a geometric point, a unit of length, and the ends of a dividing cell.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分属「轴」与「杆」两条线：地球两端、长杆、磁极与电极、对立极端、几何极点、长度单位，以及分裂细胞的两极。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an axis emerging from a turning sphere at two ends, beside a single straight rod.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条轴从旋转球体的两端穿出，旁边另立一根笔直的长杆。

branches.en: TWO ENDS: earth, magnet and battery all concentrate their force at a pair of ends.
branches.cn: 两端：地球、磁体与电池都把力集中在成对的两端。

branches.en: THE ROD: a stick becomes a tool and then a unit of length.
branches.cn: 杆：一根棍子成为工具，再成为长度单位。

branches.en: OPPOSITION: two ends facing away become a picture of extreme disagreement.
branches.cn: 对立：两端背向而居，成为极端分歧的图景。

branches.en: GEOMETRY: a circle or sphere defines a matching point on its axis.
branches.cn: 几何：圆或球在它的轴上定义一个对应的点。

branches.en: CELL: a dividing cell's spindle has two ends that pull chromosomes apart.
branches.cn: 细胞：分裂细胞的纺锤体有两端，把染色体拉向两边。

intro.en: Pole carries two Latin roots that look alike in English: polus 'axis' and palus 'stake'. Compounds such as flagpole come from the rod, while polar and polarity come from the axis.
intro.cn: pole 在英语中合并了两个外形相近的拉丁词根：polus「轴」与 palus「桩」。flagpole 等复合词来自「杆」，polar 与 polarity 来自「轴」。

latinIntro.en: Greek polos 'axis' gives Latin polus, English pole, polar and polarity; Latin palus 'stake' gives Old English pāl, English pole 'rod' and palisade.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 polos「轴」衍生拉丁 polus、英语 pole、polar 与 polarity；拉丁 palus「桩」衍生古英语 pāl、英语 pole「杆」与 palisade。

items.example: The Latin word entered English as pole.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁词进入英语作 pole。

items.example: The South Pole is colder than the coast.
A different Latin word from polus.
items.exampleCN: 这是与 polus 不同的拉丁词。

items.example: A palisade surrounded the old fort.
items.exampleCN: 旧堡垒四周有木桩栅栏。

items.example: The flagpole stands in the square.
She cleared the bar in the pole-vault.
items.exampleCN: 她在撑杆跳中越过了横杆。

definition_zh: 警方；警察部门；警察（人员）；维持治安；监督
definition_en: the official body that keeps public order and enforces the law, its members, and the act of keeping order in a place or process
core_image: 夜里扫过街角的蓝灯，行人自动让开一条路
scene: 深夜的街口，蓝灯在墙上扫来扫去，几个人被请到路边问话。The police closed the road after the accident and asked drivers to turn back.
sceneCN: 这里指「警方」这个机构整体（第 1 个义项：维持公共秩序的官方部门，作主语时谓语用复数）；句意为事故之后警方封了路，让司机掉头。画面里有夜色、街口和转动的蓝灯。

pos.zh: 警方；警察部门；警察（人员）

derivatives.zh: 由 police 与 man 复合而成，义为「男警察」
由 police 与 woman 复合而成，义为「女警察」
由 police 加 -ing 构成，义为「维持治安；警务工作」

senses.title: The official body that keeps public order
senses.definition: the official organization whose members keep order, prevent crime and enforce the law, grammatically treated as plural
senses.definitionCN: 负责维持秩序、预防犯罪、执行法律的官方机构，语法上按复数处理
senses.example: The police were called when the shop alarm went off.
senses.exampleCN: 商店警报响起来时，有人报了警。
senses.why: The word first named the whole administration of a city rather than its officers, so the institution itself owns the noun, and English keeps a plural verb after it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指一座城市的整套行政管理，而不是其中的警员；机构本身占住了名词，所以英语在它后面仍用复数谓语。

senses.title: The members of that body
senses.definition: the men and women who serve in that organization, counted as people rather than as an institution
senses.definitionCN: 在这个机构里任职的男男女女，按人而不是按机构来数
senses.example: Two police were standing at the gate all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 两名警察整个上午都站在门口。
senses.why: Because the noun names a body, the people inside the body are named by the same word with no plural ending, so institution and members share one form.
senses.whyCN: 名词既指一个整体，整体里的人就用同一个词来说，而且不加复数词尾，于是机构与成员共用一个形式。

senses.title: To keep order in a place
senses.definition: to keep order in an area by patrolling it and enforcing the rules there
senses.definitionCN: 在某片区域内巡逻并执行规则，从而维持秩序
senses.example: Extra officers were sent to police the square during the festival.
senses.exampleCN: 节日期间，另有警员被派去广场维持秩序。
senses.why: If the noun is the institution that keeps order, the verb is that institution set in motion over a piece of ground.
senses.whyCN: 如果名词是「维持秩序的机构」，动词就是让这个机构在一片地面上动起来。

senses.title: To control how an activity is carried out
senses.definition: to control how an agreement, system or set of rules is followed, often by a group watching its own members
senses.definitionCN: 管控某项协议、制度或规则如何被执行，常指团体自查自管
senses.example: The committee was asked to police its own spending more strictly.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会被要求更严格地管住自己的开支。
senses.why: Order has to be kept inside rules and budgets as well as on streets, so the same verb reaches from city squares into contracts and accounts.
senses.whyCN: 秩序不只在街上维持，也要在规则和预算里维持，所以这个动词从城市广场一直伸进合同与账目。

intro.en: Police goes back through French to a Latin word for the administration of a community, and its Greek ancestor is the same city word that also gave English policy.
intro.cn: police 经法语上溯到表示「共同体管理」的拉丁词，而它的希腊祖先是那个「城邦」词，英语的 policy 也出于此。

items.en: Polis meant a city and the body of citizens who belonged to it, and it supplied the whole vocabulary of civic life.
items.cn: polis 意为城邦以及属于它的公民群体，公民生活的一整套词汇都由它而来。

items.en: Politeia named citizenship and the constitution of a city, that is, the way a community was organized and governed.
items.cn: politeia 指公民身份与城邦政体，也就是一个共同体被组织和治理的方式。

items.en: Latin politia took over the sense of public administration, the running of a community as a whole.
items.cn: 拉丁语 politia 承接了「公共行政」这层意思，指把整个共同体管理起来。

items.en: Old French police meant public order and the administration that maintained it, still without any idea of a uniformed force.
items.cn: 古法语 police 指公共秩序以及维持它的行政机构，当时还没有穿制服的警队这层意思。

items.en: Modern English narrowed police to the body that keeps order and made it a plural collective; policy took the same root but drifted to a plan of action, so the two now share an origin and nothing else.
items.cn: 现代英语把 police 收窄为维持秩序的机构，并把它当作复数集体名词；policy 出于同一词根，却漂向「行动方案」，两者如今只在来源上相同，词义已不相干。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Greek city root; the near-meaning group gathers words for the people who keep order.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在希腊语「城邦」词根上的词；近义组收表示「维持秩序的人」的词。

entries.definition: A plan or course of action; it shares the Greek city root but long ago split from the meaning of public order.
entries.definitionCN: 政策；方针。与 police 同出希腊语「城邦」词根，但很早以前就从「公共秩序」这一义分叉出去了。

entries.definition: The activity of governing a country or city, from the same Greek word for the city.
entries.definitionCN: 政治；政治活动，同出那个表示城邦的希腊词。

entries.definition: The work of keeping order in an area.
entries.definitionCN: 在某一地区维持秩序的工作。

entries.definition: A male member of the police force.
entries.definitionCN: 男警察。

entries.definition: A person holding a position of authority, especially in the police.
entries.definitionCN: 担任职务、拥有权力的人，尤指警官。

entries.definition: A police officer of the lowest rank in Britain.
entries.definitionCN: 英国警衔最低的警员。

entries.definition: To move regularly through an area to watch for trouble.
entries.definitionCN: 在某一区域定时巡查以防范问题。

entries.definition: An elected law officer in a county, chiefly in the United States.
entries.definitionCN: 郡县里经选举产生的执法官，主要见于美国。

normalIntro.en: The word is the administration of a city seen from outside: first the running of a community, then the force that keeps its order.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是从外面看到的城市管理：先是共同体的运作，后来才是维持其秩序的队伍。

normal.en: The Greek root polis means city, so police and policy are cousins that grew up in the same town.
normal.cn: 希腊词根 polis 意为城邦，所以 police 与 policy 是在同一座城里长大的表亲。

normal.en: Policy took the planning side of that root and means a course of action, while police took the order side and means the force that keeps it.
normal.cn: policy 拿走这个词根的「筹划」一侧，指行动方针；police 拿走「秩序」一侧，指维持秩序的力量。

normal.en: The police takes a plural verb because the noun names a body of people, not one person.
normal.cn: the police 后面用复数谓语，因为名词指的是一群人，而不是一个人。

normal.en: Two police without a plural ending shows that the same form can name the members as well as the institution.
normal.cn: two police 不加复数词尾，说明同一个形式既指机构，也指机构里的成员。

normal.en: Police as a verb takes an object: you police a street, a match or a treaty, because order is always kept over something.
normal.cn: police 作动词要带宾语：police a street、a match、a treaty，因为秩序总是施加在某样东西上。

abstract.en: A word for city government turning into a word for a night patrol shows how abstract administration becomes visible on a street corner.
abstract.cn: 一个指城市行政的词变成指夜间巡逻的词，说明抽象的管理最终要在街角显形。

abstract.en: Police and policy split because a community needs both a plan and someone to enforce it.
abstract.cn: police 与 policy 分家，是因为一个共同体既需要方案，也需要有人去执行。

abstract.en: The plural verb is a small grammatical trace of the idea that order is kept by many hands, not one.
abstract.cn: 那个复数谓语是一点语法痕迹，记着「秩序由许多只手维持，而不是一只」。

examples.en: The police were called when the shop alarm went off.
examples.cn: 商店警报响起来时，有人报了警。

examples.en: Two police were standing at the gate all morning.
examples.cn: 两名警察整个上午都站在门口。

examples.en: Extra officers were sent to police the square during the festival.
examples.cn: 节日期间，另有警员被派去广场维持秩序。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坡利斯」——街口一有动静，警车爬坡就到，办事利索，这就是 police 的警方。

root: 希腊语 polis（城邦）→ politeia（公民身份、政体）→ 拉丁语 politia（公共行政）→ 古法语 police；与 policy 同源，但 policy 走的是「施政方案」一路，词义早已分叉。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the administration of a community; it narrows into the body that keeps order, then splits into its members and into the act of keeping order.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「共同体的管理」；它收窄为维持秩序的机构，再分出机构里的成员与维持秩序这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blue light sweeping a night street while people step aside to let order pass.
core.cn: 核心意象：蓝灯扫过夜里的街道，行人自动让开一条路。

branches.en: a blue light turning at a night corner
branches.cn: 夜里拐角处转动的蓝灯

branches.en: an officer writing a name into a notebook
branches.cn: 警员把姓名记进本子

branches.en: a line of officers walking across a square
branches.cn: 一队警员横穿广场

branches.en: a committee reading a budget line by line
branches.cn: 委员会逐行核对预算

branches.en: a station desk crowded at midnight
branches.cn: 午夜挤满人的警局值班台

intro.en: A Greek word for the city, its abstract noun of citizenship, and a Latin noun of administration hold this family together, with English splitting it into the body, the members and the task.
intro.cn: 一个希腊语的「城邦」词、它表示公民身份的抽象名词，以及一个拉丁语的管理名词，共同撑起这一族；英语再把它分成机构、成员与任务。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: to keep order in a place

definition_zh: 男警察；警员
definition_en: a man who is a member of the police force; a male police officer
core_image: 街角站着一名穿制服的男警，帽檐压得很正，手按在腰间的对讲机上
scene: 路口红灯坏了，车流乱成一团。A policeman stepped into the crossing and began to wave the cars through.
sceneCN: 这里 policeman 是「男警察」（第 1 个义项：警察队伍里的男性成员）；句意为一名男警察走到斑马线上，开始挥手指挥车辆通行。

derivatives.zh: 由 police 与 woman 复合而成，义为「女警察」
复合词的基础词，义为「警方；警察部门」
由 police 加 -ing 构成，义为「警务工作；维持治安」

senses.title: A male member of the police force
senses.definition: a man whose job is to keep order, enforce the law and help the public as a member of the police
senses.definitionCN: 以维持秩序、执行法律、帮助公众为职业的男性，属于警察队伍
senses.example: A policeman helped the old lady across the road.
senses.exampleCN: 一名男警察扶老太太过了马路。
senses.why: Police names the force as a whole, and man turns it into one person you can point at on the street.
senses.whyCN: police 指整支警察队伍，man 把它落到街上可以指着的一个具体的人身上。

senses.title: A figure of order and help
senses.definition: a person seen as the symbol of law and order, or the one you turn to when there is trouble
senses.definitionCN: 被视为法律与秩序象征的人，或出了事时大家去求助的那个人
senses.example: Every child on the street knows the policeman at the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 街上的每个孩子都认识街角那位警察。
senses.why: Because the job is standing in public with authority, the word also names the trusted figure that stands for order, not just the man in uniform.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个职业就是带着权威站在公众面前，这个词也用来指秩序本身的象征，不只是那身制服下的一个人。

intro.en: Policeman is an English compound: police, borrowed through French from a Greek word for the city and its administration, joined to man.
intro.cn: policeman 是英语复合词：police 经法语借自希腊语中表示城市及其行政的词，再与 man 复合。

items.en: Greek polis named a city or city-state, and its affairs: citizenship, administration, public order.
items.cn: 希腊语 polis 指城市或城邦，也指城市的事务：公民身份、行政、公共秩序。

items.en: From polis came politeia, the condition and organization of the citizen body, government of a city.
items.cn: 由 polis 派生出 politeia，指公民共同体的状态与组织方式，即城邦的治理。

items.en: Latin took over politeia as politia, keeping the sense of civil administration and government.
items.cn: 拉丁语吸收了 politeia 作 politia，保留公民行政与治理的含义。

items.en: Old French police meant the ordering and government of a community before it narrowed to the force that keeps order.
items.cn: 古法语 police 先指对共同体的治理与秩序安排，后来才缩小到维持秩序的那支队伍。

items.en: English compounded police with man to make policeman, one identifiable male officer of that force, with the irregular plural policemen.
items.cn: 英语把 police 与 man 复合成 policeman，指这支队伍中一名可以辨认的男性警员，复数为不规则形式 policemen。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the compound family and one word that only echoes the ending; the near-meaning group gathers people of the same calling.
note.cn: 形近组收同一个复合词族的词，另收一个只是词尾相像的词；近义组收同一职业的各类人员。

entries.definition: A female member of the police force, the feminine counterpart of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 警察队伍中的女性成员，是这个词的阴性对应形式。

entries.definition: The police force itself, or its members collectively; the first element of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 警方、警察队伍整体；复合词的第一个成分。

entries.definition: A member of a fire brigade; built with the same -man pattern but a different calling.
entries.definitionCN: 消防队员；用同样的 -man 构词方式，但职业不同。

entries.definition: A man of good manners or birth; it shares the -man ending and the irregular plural pattern but has a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 绅士、有教养的男士；共享 -man 词尾与不规则复数模式，但来源不同。

entries.definition: A person holding a position of authority, often used of police officers.
entries.definitionCN: 担任权威职务的人，常用来指警官。

entries.definition: An informal word for a police officer.
entries.definitionCN: 警察的非正式说法。

entries.definition: A police officer of the lowest rank, common in British usage.
entries.definitionCN: 级别最低的警察，英式常用说法。

normalIntro.en: The word is a straightforward compound, and everything in the family repeats the same two-part picture: a force, plus the man who wears it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是直白的复合词，词族里反复出现同一个两段式画面：一支队伍，加上穿着它的那个人。

normal.en: Police comes from Greek polis, the city, so a policeman is literally a man of the city's order.
normal.cn: police 来自希腊语 polis（城市），所以 policeman 字面上就是「城邦秩序之人」。

normal.en: Police + man, force + person: the compound says the whole force in one man.
normal.cn: police + man，队伍 + 人：这个复合词用一个人代表整支队伍。

normal.en: The plural is irregular: policeman becomes policemen, exactly like man becoming men.
normal.cn: 复数不规则：policeman 变 policemen，与 man 变 men 完全一致。

normal.en: The same pattern gives policewoman, fireman and postman, so once you know one you know the family.
normal.cn: 同样的构词法给出 policewoman、fireman、postman，认识一个就认识一族。

normal.en: Police is collective and takes a plural verb in British English; policeman is a single, countable person.
normal.cn: police 是集合名词，英式英语中常配复数动词；policeman 则是可数的单个人。

abstract.en: A policeman is order given a face: where he stands, the street agrees on the rules.
abstract.cn: 警察是有面孔的秩序：他站在哪里，哪条街就认同规则。

abstract.en: Calling a policeman is turning private fear into public procedure.
abstract.cn: 叫警察，就是把个人的害怕变成公开的程序。

abstract.en: The uniform erases the person and leaves only the order he carries.
abstract.cn: 制服抹掉个人，只留下他所携带的秩序。

examples.en: A policeman helped the old lady across the road.
examples.cn: 一名男警察扶老太太过了马路。

examples.en: The policemen on patrol found the lost child in the park.
examples.cn: 巡逻的警察们在公园里找到了走失的孩子。

examples.en: If you lose your way at night, ask a policeman for directions.
examples.cn: 晚上迷路的话，向警察问路。

root: policeman 由 police 与 man 复合而成；police 经古法语 police（公共行政、秩序）上溯拉丁语 politia，最终源自希腊语 polis（城邦），与 policy 同源但词义早已分叉。

sensesIntro.en: The compound takes a whole force and puts it into one street-level person; the senses run from the man in uniform to the idea of order he stands for.
sensesIntro.cn: 复合词把整支队伍装进一个街头层面的人身上；义项从穿制服的那个人，走到他所代表的秩序观念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a man in uniform at a street corner, his hand on the crossing signal.
core.cn: 核心意象：街角穿制服的男人，手按在路口的指挥信号上。

branches.en: a lost child led by the hand to the station

intro.en: The compound is English-made, but its first half carries a Greek word for the city all the way through French and Latin.
intro.cn: 复合词本身是英语造的，但前一半带着一个希腊语的「城邦」词，一路经过法语和拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: The Greek politeia passed into Latin as politia; that Latin form is the recorded carrier of the word into Romance, so it is listed as the linking entry.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 politeia 进入拉丁语作 politia；这个拉丁形式是该词进入罗曼语族的记录载体，列为承转条目。

definition_zh: 政策；方针；原则；保险单；（古）治国术
definition_en: a course of action or set of principles adopted by a government or organization; a written contract of insurance
core_image: 一群人先定下走哪条路，再让所有人照这条路走
scene: 政府宣布了一项关于碳排放的新政策。The government announced a new policy on carbon emissions.
sceneCN: 这里 policy 是「政府采取的行动方针」（第 1 个义项：政策）；句意：政府宣布了一项关于碳排放的新政策。场景要点：公共决定、成文、要被执行；对应第 1 个义项。
